ok: Because the leader gets no such help, birds take turns at the front, sharing the hardest position.

kanca.ow: the leader gets no such help

kanca.pw: behind and to the side of another

d.t: This rising air is created by the tips of the wings as each bird pushes down.
d.key: a swirl of rising air near the tips of its wings
d.bait: This rising air is created by the tips of the wings
d.why: Yükselen havanın kaynağı ikinci cümlenin işi. Sonda yeniden mekanizmaya dönülünce paragraf ileri gitmek yerine başa sarıyor.

d.t: By flapping in step with the bird in front, each one made the most of the lift it received.
d.key: timed their wingbeats to match the bird ahead
d.bait: flapping in step with the bird in front
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Yeni bir şey eklemiyor; özellikle öndeki kuşun bu yardımı alamaması sorunu açıkta kalıyor.

d.t: Ibises were once common across Europe but are now among the world's most endangered birds.
d.why: Konu ibislerin nesline kayıyor. Ibis yalnızca araştırmanın aracı; paragraf V düzeninin işleyişini anlatıyor.

d.t: This rotation is especially important on the longest flights, such as those across seas and deserts.
d.why: 'This rotation' karşılıksız: paragrafta sırayla öne geçmekten hiç söz edilmedi.

yol: Paragraf arkadaki kuşların bedava kaldırma aldığını anlatıyor. Okuyucunun aklına gelen soru: peki en öndeki? Son cümle bunu cevaplamalı: öndeki yardım almaz, bu yüzden kuşlar sırayla öne geçer. 'no such help' doğrudan 'free lift'e işaret ediyor.

p: In the 1960s, the psychologist Robert Zajonc showed people a series of made-up words, some of them only once and others up to twenty-five times.
The participants were not told what the words meant.
Repeated exposure alone, it seemed, had made the words more likeable.
This mere exposure effect has since been found with faces, music, shapes and even Chinese characters shown to people who could not read them.
It may explain why a song we disliked at first can grow on us after we have heard it a few times on the radio.
ok: Yet when later asked which words meant something good, they mostly chose the ones they had seen most often.

kanca.ow: the ones they had seen most often

kanca.pw: were not told what the words meant
kanca.ow: Yet when later asked which words meant something good

d.t: For this reason, they tended to rate the most frequently shown words as having the most pleasant meanings.
d.key: The participants were not told what the words meant.
d.why: İçerik yerinde ama bağlaç yanlış. Anlamların söylenmemesi, sık görülen kelimelerin olumlu seçilmesinin SEBEBİ değil; tam tersine, buna RAĞMEN olan şaşırtıcı bir sonuç. 'Yet' gerekir.

d.t: These faces were flashed on a screen so briefly that the participants did not realise they had seen them.
d.why: 'These faces' karşılıksız: deneyde yüz değil kelime var; yüzler ancak sonraki araştırmaları anan cümlede geçiyor.

d.t: They had no idea, therefore, whether any of these strange new words had a pleasant or an unpleasant meaning.
d.key: The participants were not told what the words meant.
d.bait: no idea, therefore, whether any of these strange new words
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Deneyin sonucunu vermediği için sonraki 'Repeated exposure alone had made the words more likeable' hangi bulguya dayandığını gösteremiyor.

d.t: The same effect has since been found with music, faces, shapes and many other kinds of stimulus.
d.key: has since been found with faces, music, shapes
d.bait: has since been found with music, faces, shapes
d.why: Sonraki araştırmalar beşinci cümlenin işi. Asıl deneyin sonucu söylenmeden 'aynı etki' başka alanlara taşınıyor; 'the same effect' henüz ortada olmayan bir etkiye işaret ediyor.

yol: Önceki cümle 'anlamları söylenmedi' diyor; sonraki 'yalnız tekrar, kelimeleri sevimli kıldı' diye bir SONUÇ yorumluyor. Arada bulgu olmalı: anlamı bilmedikleri hâlde ('Yet') en sık gördüklerini olumlu seçtiler.

p: The body's main defence against overheating is sweat.
As sweat evaporates from the skin, it carries heat away with it, cooling the body underneath.
It simply drips off the skin, and much of its cooling power is lost.
This is why a hot, humid day can be more dangerous than a hotter but drier one.
Older people are especially at risk, since they tend to sweat less and may not feel thirsty even when they need to drink.
Health services in many countries now issue warnings based on both temperature and humidity.
ok: In very humid weather, however, the air is already so full of moisture that sweat evaporates only slowly.

kanca.pw: As sweat evaporates from the skin
It simply drips off the skin

d.t: For example, on a humid day the air is so full of water that sweat can hardly evaporate.
d.key: As sweat evaporates from the skin, it carries heat away
d.why: İçerik yerinde ama bağlaç yanlış. Nemli hava, terle serinlemenin bir ÖRNEĞİ değil, onun işlemediği İSTİSNA; burada 'however' gerekir.

d.t: In humid weather, this process works even better, since the damp air draws sweat off the skin faster.
d.key: much of its cooling power is lost
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki cümle terin damlayıp gittiğini ve serinletme gücünün KAYBOLDUĞUNU söylüyor; nem süreci iyileştirmiyor, bozuyor.

d.t: The evaporation of water from the skin, then, is what keeps our temperature under control.
d.key: As sweat evaporates from the skin, it carries heat away
d.bait: is what keeps our temperature under control
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Buharlaşmanın ne zaman AKSADIĞINI söylemediği için sonraki 'It simply drips off the skin' anlamsız kalıyor.

d.t: Some people sweat far more heavily than others, a difference that seems to be partly inherited.
d.why: Konu kişiler arası terleme farkına kayıyor. Paragraf nemin terlemeyi nasıl etkisiz kıldığını anlatıyor; sonraki cümle damlayıp giden teri bekliyor.

yol: Önceki cümle kuralı veriyor: ter buharlaşınca serinletir. Sonraki cümle 'damlayıp gidiyor, serinletme gücü kayboluyor' diyor. Arada kuralın BOZULDUĞU durum olmalı: nemli havada ter buharlaşamıyor. Beşinci cümledeki 'humid day' de bunu doğruluyor.

p: Emperor penguins breed during the Antarctic winter, when temperatures can fall below minus 40 degrees and winds blow at great speed.
The males incubate the eggs on their feet for about two months without eating, so they must save every bit of energy they can.
Their solution is to press together in huddles of hundreds or even thousands of birds.
Inside a dense huddle, the temperature can rise above 20 degrees, which is warmer than the birds actually need.
The huddle is constantly moving, as birds on the cold outer edge gradually work their way towards the centre and others are pushed out.
ok: Few animals in the world face harsher conditions while raising their young than the emperor penguin does.

kanca.pw: temperatures can fall below minus 40 degrees

d.t: This huddle can contain thousands of birds packed so tightly that they can hardly move.
d.why: Paragraf 'This huddle' ile açılamaz; sürü hâlinde toplanma ancak dördüncü cümlede tanıtılıyor.

d.t: As a result, emperor penguins spend most of the year far out at sea, feeding on fish and squid.
d.why: Paragraf 'As a result' ile açılamaz; sonucu olacağı bir sebep önünde yok. Denizde beslenme de paragrafın konusu değil.

d.t: Huddling together allows the birds to save energy and survive the long, freezing winter.
d.key: Their solution is to press together in huddles
d.bait: Huddling together allows the birds to save energy
d.why: Çözüm sorundan önce geliyor. Dördüncü cümle 'Their solution' diye çözümü İLK KEZ sunuyor; başta verilirse o cümle tekrara düşer, sorun-çözüm sırası bozulur.

d.t: Emperor penguins avoid the worst of the cold by breeding during the mild Antarctic summer.
d.key: breed during the Antarctic winter
d.bait: breeding during the mild Antarctic summer
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki cümle penguenlerin tam da Antarktika KIŞINDA ürediğini söylüyor.

yol: Boşluk başta. Paragrafın iskeleti: koşullar (−40, rüzgâr, iki ay aç) → çözüm (sürü) → sürünün işleyişi. Açılış genel çerçeveyi vermeli: yavru büyütürken bu kadar zor koşullara katlanan hayvan az.

p: For thousands of years, people traded using lumps of precious metal, which had to be weighed and tested every time they changed hands.
This was slow, and it was easy to be cheated by someone who had mixed cheaper metals into the gold or silver.
The stamp guaranteed the weight and purity of each piece, so buyers and sellers no longer had to check it themselves.
These first coins spread quickly to the Greek cities and, within a few centuries, across much of the ancient world.
Coins made trade faster and safer, and they would remain the main form of money for over two thousand years.
ok: Around 600 BC, the kingdom of Lydia found a solution: small pieces of metal stamped with a royal mark.

kanca.pw: This was slow, and it was easy to be cheated

d.t: Weighing and testing the metal at every single sale, in short, made trade both slow and rather risky.
d.key: This was slow, and it was easy to be cheated
d.bait: made trade both slow and rather risky
d.why: Önceki iki cümleyi özetleyerek yineliyor. Çözümü getirmediği için sonraki 'The stamp' hangi damgadan söz ettiğini bulamıyor.

d.t: These coins soon spread to the nearby Greek cities and from there, over the following centuries, across the ancient world.
d.key: These first coins spread quickly to the Greek cities
d.why: Yayılma beşinci cümlenin işi. Sikke henüz İCAT EDİLMEDEN yayılması anlatılıyor; 'These coins' da karşılıksız kalıyor.

d.t: Gold was especially valued because, unlike iron or copper, it never rusts and keeps its shine for centuries.
d.bait: never rusts and keeps its shine
d.why: Konu altının özelliklerine kayıyor. Paragraf bir sorunu (tartma, hile) ve çözümünü (sikke) anlatıyor; sonraki 'The stamp' bir damga bekliyor.

d.t: This mark was usually the head of a lion, the symbol of the Lydian royal family.
d.why: 'This mark' karşılıksız: paragrafta henüz bir işaret ya da damga tanıtılmadı; Lidya'nın çözümü atlanmış oluyor.

yol: Önceki iki cümle bir SORUN kuruyor: tartmak yavaş, hile kolay. Sonraki cümle 'The stamp' ile bir damgadan söz ediyor. Boşluk çözümü ve damgayı tanıtmalı: Lidya, kraliyet damgalı metal parçaları.

p: Many people believe that stepping on a rusty nail causes tetanus, a serious disease that makes the muscles stiffen painfully.
In fact, rust itself is completely harmless to the body.
Tetanus is caused by a bacterium whose spores live in soil, dust and animal waste, and can survive there for years.
Old nails lying outdoors are often both rusty and dirty, which is probably how the two became linked in people's minds.
A deep puncture wound is especially risky, because the bacterium grows best where there is little oxygen.
ok: What matters, then, is not rust but how deep and dirty the wound is, and whether vaccinations are up to date.

kanca.pw: A deep puncture wound is especially risky
kanca.ow: how deep and dirty the wound is

kanca.pw: spores live in soil, dust and animal waste

d.t: Even so, a deep and dirty wound is the real danger, whatever the object was made of, and vaccination protects against it.
d.key: A deep puncture wound is especially risky
d.why: İçerik yerinde ama bağlaç yanlış. 'Even so' (yine de) bir karşıtlık bekler; oysa bu cümle önceki bilgilerin ÖZETİ ve sonucu, onlara karşı çıkmıyor.

d.t: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and water, which is why it appears faster in damp climates.
d.why: Konu pasın kimyasına kayıyor. Paragraf pasın zararsız olduğunu zaten söyledi; son cümle asıl riskin ne olduğunu toparlamalı.

d.t: A rusty nail is therefore far more dangerous than a dirty one, whatever the depth of the wound.
d.key: rust itself is completely harmless
d.bait: far more dangerous than a dirty one
d.why: Yön ters. Paragraf pasın zararsız, kirin ve derinliğin tehlikeli olduğunu anlatıyor; bu cümle her ikisini de tersine çeviriyor.

d.t: The spores of the bacterium, in short, are found mainly in soil, dust and the droppings of animals.
d.key: spores live in soil, dust and animal waste
d.bait: found mainly in soil, dust and the droppings of animals
d.why: Üçüncü cümleyi yineliyor. Paragraf bir yanılgıyı düzeltmeye başladı; son cümle doğrusunu toparlamalı, eski bir bilgiyi tekrarlamamalı.

yol: Paragraf bir yanılgıyla açılıyor (paslı çivi tetanoz yapar) ve adım adım düzeltiyor: pas zararsız → bakteri toprakta → derin yara riskli. Son cümle 'then' ile doğru kuralı toparlamalı: önemli olan pas değil, yaranın derinliği ve kiri, bir de aşı.

p: On a cold morning, a metal door handle feels much colder to the touch than a wooden door, even though both have been in the same room all night.
In fact, they are at exactly the same temperature.
Metal is an excellent conductor, so it pulls warmth from your fingers rapidly, and your nerves register this loss as cold.
Wood conducts heat poorly, so the skin touching it stays warm, and it feels only slightly cool.
What we sense, in other words, is not temperature itself but the rate at which our bodies are losing heat.
ok: The real difference lies in how quickly each material draws heat away from the skin that touches it.

kanca.pw: pulls warmth from your fingers rapidly
kanca.ow: how quickly each material draws heat away

kanca.pw: the rate at which our bodies are losing heat

d.t: This conductor carries the heat of your hand away far faster than most other materials.
d.why: 'This conductor' karşılıksız: iletken kavramı ancak sonraki cümlede geçiyor. Önce iki malzemenin farkının nereden geldiği söylenmeli.

d.t: Our skin, it turns out, senses the speed at which heat is lost rather than the temperature itself.
d.key: is not temperature itself but the rate at which our bodies are losing heat
d.bait: senses the speed at which heat is lost
d.why: Bu, paragrafın vardığı genel sonuç; son cümlenin işi. Metal ve tahta örnekleri anlatılmadan sonuç önden veriliyor.

d.t: A thermometer placed against each of them would show exactly the same reading on its scale.
d.key: they are at exactly the same temperature
d.bait: would show exactly the same reading
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Farkın NEREDEN geldiğine geçmediği için sonraki metal-iletken açıklaması bağlamsız kalıyor.

d.t: As a result, the metal and the wood end up drawing heat away from the skin at very different speeds.
d.key: they are at exactly the same temperature
d.why: İçerik yerinde ama bağlaç yanlış. İki malzemenin aynı sıcaklıkta olması, ısıyı farklı hızda çekmelerinin SEBEBİ değil; fark malzemenin kendisinden geliyor.

yol: Önceki cümle bir bilmece kuruyor: hissedilen fark var ama sıcaklık aynı. Sonraki iki cümle metal ve tahtayı ısıyı çekme HIZIYLA açıklıyor. Boşluk bu açıklamayı haber vermeli: fark, ısıyı ne kadar hızlı çektiklerinde.

p: Imagine being told by your doctor that a surgical operation has a 90 per cent survival rate.
Now imagine being told instead that it has a 10 per cent death rate.
In studies, patients and even experienced doctors were noticeably more willing to choose the operation when it was described in terms of survival.
Psychologists call this the framing effect: the way a choice is presented can change the decision, even when the facts are identical.
For this reason, some medical experts recommend giving patients both versions of the figures, so that neither one dominates.
ok: The two statements mean exactly the same thing, yet people react to them very differently.

kanca.ow: The two statements mean exactly the same thing

kanca.pw: more willing to choose the operation
even when the facts are identical

d.t: Psychologists refer to this as the framing effect, and it influences many everyday choices.
d.key: Psychologists call this the framing effect
d.bait: Psychologists refer to this as the framing effect
d.why: Etkinin adı beşinci cümlenin işi. Araştırma bulgusu verilmeden ad konuyor; 'this' de henüz gösterilmemiş bir etkiye işaret ediyor.

d.t: The second statement, however, clearly describes a far riskier operation than the first one, which sounds reassuring.
d.key: even when the facts are identical
d.why: Yön ters. %90 yaşam ile %10 ölüm AYNI bilgidir; paragraf tam da olguların aynı olduğunu ('facts are identical') vurguluyor.

d.t: These doctors were then asked which version they would prefer to hear as patients.
d.why: 'These doctors' karşılıksız: doktorlar ancak sonraki cümlede, araştırmayla birlikte anılıyor.

d.t: Survival rates for many common operations have improved greatly over the past fifty years.
d.bait: have improved greatly over the past fifty years
d.why: Konu tıbbın ilerlemesine kayıyor. Paragraf aynı bilginin iki farklı SUNUMUNU karşılaştırıyor.

yol: İlk iki cümle aynı bilgiyi iki biçimde veriyor. Sonraki cümle insanların bunlara farklı tepki verdiğini gösteriyor; beşinci cümle 'facts are identical' diyor. Boşluk ikisini bağlar: anlam aynı, tepki farklı.

p: For decades, people were advised to eat no more than a few eggs a week, because a single yolk contains a large amount of cholesterol.
High levels of cholesterol in the blood are linked to heart disease, so the advice seemed to make sense.
Later research, however, showed that for most people, the cholesterol in food has only a modest effect on the level in the blood.
The liver makes most of the body's cholesterol itself and tends to make less when more comes from the diet.
As a result, many health organisations have dropped strict limits on eggs, while still advising caution for some patients.
ok: Few everyday foods have seen their reputation change as dramatically over the years as the humble egg.

kanca.pw: For decades, people were advised to eat no more than a few eggs a week

d.t: On the other hand, eggs are an excellent source of protein and several important vitamins.
d.why: Paragraf 'On the other hand' ile açılamaz; karşısına konacak 'bir yandan' yok. Besin değeri de paragrafın izlediği değişim hikâyesi değil.

d.t: This advice was based mainly on the fact that egg yolks are rich in fat.
d.why: Paragraf 'This advice' ile açılamaz; tavsiye ancak ikinci cümlede veriliyor. Üstelik tavsiyenin gerekçesi yağ değil kolesteroldü.

d.t: The liver, after all, produces most of the cholesterol in the body on its own.
d.key: The liver makes most of the body's cholesterol itself
d.why: Karaciğer bilgisi beşinci cümlenin işi; 'after all' de önceden kurulmuş bir iddiaya dayanır. Başta gelince açıklama, açıklanacak şeyden önce geliyor.

d.t: Chickens were first domesticated in Asia several thousand years ago, probably for cockfighting rather than for their meat or eggs.
d.why: Odak tavuğun evcilleştirilmesine kayıyor. Paragrafın konusu yumurta tavsiyesinin nasıl DEĞİŞTİĞİ.

yol: Boşluk başta. Paragrafın iskeleti: onlarca yıl kısıtlama → yeni araştırma → kısıtlamalar kalktı. Açılış bu DEĞİŞİMİ haber vermeli; 'For decades' ve 'have dropped' arasındaki köprü bu.

p: If a human loses a finger, it is gone for good, but the axolotl, a Mexican salamander, can regrow entire legs.
It can also rebuild parts of its heart, spinal cord and even brain without leaving any scar.
Within weeks, this bud grows into a new limb, complete with bones, muscles and nerves in the right places.
Scientists hope that by understanding how these cells 'know' what to rebuild, they may one day help human wounds heal with less scarring.
Sadly, the axolotl is almost extinct in the wild, surviving mainly in a few canals near Mexico City.
ok: After an injury, cells near the wound lose their specialised identity and gather into a bud of tissue.

d.t: Its ability to repair itself, in short, goes far beyond that of any human.
d.key: If a human loses a finger, it is gone for good
d.bait: goes far beyond that of any human
d.why: İlk iki cümleyi özetleyerek yineliyor. Onarımın NASIL başladığını söylemediği için sonraki 'this bud' hangi tomurcuğa işaret ettiğini bulamıyor.

d.t: After an injury, a thick scar quickly forms over the wound, sealing it off for good.
d.key: without leaving any scar
d.why: Yön ters. Önceki cümle aksolotlun İZ BIRAKMADAN onardığını söylüyor; kalın bir yara izi yeni uzvun büyümesini de engeller.

d.t: Scientists are now studying these cells in the hope of improving how human wounds heal.
d.key: Scientists hope that by understanding how these cells
d.bait: Scientists are now studying these cells
d.why: Bilim insanlarının umudu beşinci cümlenin işi. Hücrelerin ne yaptığı anlatılmadan araştırmaya geçiliyor; 'these cells' de karşılıksız kalıyor.

d.t: As a result, cells near the wound lose their special roles and form a small bud of new tissue.
d.key: rebuild parts of its heart, spinal cord and even brain
d.why: İçerik yerinde ama bağlaç yanlış. Hücrelerin tomurcuk oluşturması bu yeteneğin SONUCU değil, onu mümkün kılan MEKANİZMA; sebep-sonuç ters kurulmuş.

yol: Sonraki cümlede 'this bud', beşinci cümlede 'these cells' var: boşluk hem hücreleri hem tomurcuğu tanıtmalı. Önceki cümleler yeteneği anlattı; boşluk sürecin İLK adımını vermeli: yaranın yanındaki hücreler özelliklerini kaybedip tomurcuk oluşturur.

p: In the 1880s, the French engineer Max Ringelmann asked men to pull on a rope, first alone and then in groups.
One might expect eight men to pull eight times as hard as one.
In fact, each man in a group of eight pulled with less than half the force he had used alone.
Later studies ruled out poor coordination as the main cause: even people who only believed they were in a team made less effort.
When individual contributions cannot be seen or measured, it seems, people quietly hold back.
ok: This tendency, now called social loafing, is weaker when each member's work is visible and counted separately.

kanca.pw: When individual contributions cannot be seen or measured
kanca.ow: when each member's work is visible and counted separately

d.t: These blindfolded volunteers pulled hardest of all when they thought that nobody else was on the rope.
d.why: 'These blindfolded volunteers' karşılıksız: paragrafta gözü bağlı gönüllülerden hiç söz edilmedi.

d.t: Tug of war was an Olympic sport until 1920, when it was dropped from the programme.
d.why: Konu halat çekmenin spor tarihine kayıyor. Paragraf grupta harcanan çabayı anlatıyor; son cümle bu eğilimi adlandırmalı ya da çözümünü vermeli.

d.t: Hidden in a crowd, in short, many people tend to put in less effort than they would alone.
d.key: people quietly hold back
d.bait: put in less effort than they would alone
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Eğilime ad vermiyor, onu azaltan koşulu da söylemiyor; paragraf yerinde sayıyor.

d.t: Working as part of a team, therefore, almost always makes each individual member try harder than when working alone.
d.key: each man in a group of eight pulled with less than half the force
d.bait: makes each individual member try harder
d.why: Yön ters. Deneylerin bulgusu grupta kişi başı çabanın AZALDIĞI; ekipte daha çok çalışıldığını söylemek bunu tersine çeviriyor.

yol: Önceki cümle genel bir yorum yaptı: katkı görünmeyince insanlar geri durur. Son cümle bu eğilime ad vermeli ve 'görünmeyince' koşulunun tersini kurmalı: katkı görünür ve ayrı sayılırsa eğilim zayıflar.

p: Many people still begin a workout by holding long, static stretches, such as touching their toes for thirty seconds or more.
The habit is based on the belief that stretching a cold muscle protects it from injury.
Holding a stretch for a long time may even reduce a muscle's strength and power for a short while afterwards.
For this reason, many coaches now recommend a dynamic warm-up instead: gentle jogging, leg swings and other movements that gradually raise the heart rate.
Static stretching still has a place, but it seems better suited to the end of a session.
ok: Large reviews of the research, however, have found little evidence that stretching before exercise prevents injuries.

d.t: Coaches therefore now tend to favour a dynamic warm-up, such as gentle jogging, skipping and leg swings.
d.key: many coaches now recommend a dynamic warm-up instead
d.bait: Coaches therefore now tend to favour a dynamic warm-up
d.why: Antrenörlerin tavsiyesi beşinci cümlenin işi. İnancın YANLIŞ olduğu gösterilmeden çözüme geçiliyor; 'therefore' neye dayandığını gösteremiyor.

d.t: Similarly, scientific reviews have found little sign that stretching before a workout prevents injuries.
d.key: The habit is based on the belief
d.why: İçerik yerinde ama bağlaç yanlış. Araştırma bulgusu inanca BENZEMİYOR, onu çürütüyor; 'Similarly' yerine 'however' gerekir.

d.t: Flexibility tends to decline with age, especially in people who spend most of the day sitting.
d.why: Konu yaşla azalan esnekliğe kayıyor. Paragraf bir inancın sınanmasını anlatıyor; sonraki 'may even reduce' önce bir 'yararı yok' bulgusu bekliyor.

d.t: A muscle that is stretched while still cold, many people assume, is less likely to tear.
d.key: stretching a cold muscle protects it from injury
d.why: Önceki cümledeki inancı yineliyor. Sonraki cümledeki 'even' (hatta) bir adım ötesine geçer; önce 'koruduğu kanıtlanmadı' denmeli ki 'hatta zarar verebilir' anlam kazansın.

yol: Önceki cümle bir İNANÇ veriyor. Sonraki cümle 'may even reduce' diyor: 'even' (hatta) önceki cümlenin zaten olumsuz bir şey söylediğini gösterir. Boşluk inancı sarsmalı: araştırmalar germenin sakatlığı önlediğine dair az kanıt buldu.

p: When it rises above the horizon, the full moon often looks enormous, yet a few hours later, high in the sky, it seems to have shrunk.
Photographs show that its size has not changed at all; if anything, it is very slightly larger when it is overhead.
The effect, known as the moon illusion, takes place entirely inside our heads.
Its exact cause is still debated, but one common explanation is that the brain judges the horizon to be farther away than the sky overhead.
A moon near trees and buildings on the distant horizon is therefore interpreted as a much bigger object.
ok: The moon is one of the most familiar sights in the sky, yet it plays a curious trick on us.

kanca.pw: takes place entirely inside our heads
kanca.ow: plays a curious trick on us

kanca.pw: the full moon often looks enormous

d.t: This illusion has puzzled thinkers and scientists since at least the time of Aristotle.
d.why: Paragraf 'This illusion' ile açılamaz; yanılsama ancak sonraki cümlede anlatılıyor, adı da dördüncü cümlede konuyor.

d.t: The brain, it seems, treats the horizon as farther away than the sky directly above us.
d.key: the brain judges the horizon to be farther away than the sky overhead
d.bait: treats the horizon as farther away
d.why: Bu açıklama beşinci cümlenin işi. Yanılsama anlatılmadan sebebine geçiliyor; açıklama, açıklanacak olaydan önce geliyor.

d.t: The moon really does appear larger near the horizon, because it is closer to us at that time.
d.key: its size has not changed at all
d.bait: because it is closer to us at that time
d.why: Yön ters. Fotoğraflar boyutun DEĞİŞMEDİĞİNİ, hatta tepedeyken biraz daha büyük olduğunu gösteriyor; olay tamamen kafamızın içinde.

d.t: However, the moon is in fact no bigger near the horizon than it is when high in the sky overhead.
d.why: Paragraf 'However' ile açılamaz; karşı çıkacağı bir önceki söz yok. Bilgi de üçüncü cümlenin işi.

yol: Boşluk başta. Paragraf bir yanılsamayı anlatıyor: ufukta büyük, tepede küçük → aslında aynı → olay kafamızda. Açılış konuyu (Ay) ve yönü (bizi kandırıyor) haber vermeli; 'inside our heads' ile 'plays a trick on us' örtüşüyor.

p: In almost any park, you can find narrow strips of worn grass where people have cut across a corner instead of following the paved path.
Planners call these 'desire paths', because they show where people actually want to walk.
For a long time, the usual response was to put up fences or signs telling people to keep off the grass.
Such barriers were often ignored, and new paths soon appeared beside them.
Some universities have tried a different approach, waiting a few months after a new building opens to see where students walk.
ok: Only then do they lay paving along the routes that the students' feet have already marked out.

kanca.ow: the routes that the students' feet have already marked out

kanca.pw: they show where people actually want to walk

d.t: Grass is also far cheaper to maintain than concrete and helps rainwater soak into the ground.
d.bait: helps rainwater soak into the ground
d.why: Konu çimin yararlarına kayıyor. Önceki cümle yeni bir yaklaşım başlattı (bekle ve izle); son cümle bu yaklaşımın nasıl SONUÇLANDIĞINI vermeli.

d.t: Fences and warning signs, by contrast, were usually ignored by walkers in a hurry to get somewhere.
d.key: Such barriers were often ignored
d.bait: Fences and warning signs, by contrast
d.why: Çitlerin işe yaramadığı dördüncü cümlede zaten söylendi; sonda yeniden eski yönteme dönmek sırayı bozuyor. Yeni yaklaşım yarım kalıyor.

d.t: In this way, they can find out which routes across the campus students naturally prefer to take.
d.key: to see where students walk
d.bait: which routes across the campus students naturally prefer
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor; 'öğrencilerin nereden yürüdüğünü görmek' zaten söylendi. Bu bilgiyle NE yapıldığı eksik.

d.t: This second building was then designed entirely around the paths that had already appeared beside the first one.
d.why: 'This second building' karşılıksız: paragrafta ikinci bir binadan hiç söz edilmedi.

yol: Paragraf bir sorun (kestirme patikalar) ve başarısız bir çözüm (çit) anlattı; sonra 'a different approach' geldi: birkaç ay bekleyip izlemek. Son cümle bu yaklaşımın ikinci adımını vermeli: 'Only then' yolu ayakların açtığı yere döşerler.

p: When a drug company develops a new medicine, it is usually given a patent that prevents other firms from copying it for around twenty years.
During this time, the company can set a high price to recover the enormous cost of research.
These must contain the same active ingredient in the same amount and be shown to work in the body in the same way.
Their colour, shape or filling may differ, which sometimes makes patients suspicious.
Yet generics often cost a fraction of the original price, saving health systems large sums every year.
ok: Once the patent expires, however, other manufacturers are free to make cheaper versions, known as generics.

kanca.pw: prevents other firms from copying it
kanca.ow: other manufacturers are free to make cheaper versions

d.t: For example, other companies may then start producing cheaper copies of it, which are called generics.
d.key: the company can set a high price
d.why: İçerik yerinde ama bağlaç yanlış. Ucuz kopyalar yüksek fiyatın bir ÖRNEĞİ değil; patent bitince başlayan YENİ dönem. Burada 'however' gerekir.

d.t: Even after the patent expires, no other firm is allowed to make the medicine.
d.key: These must contain the same active ingredient
d.bait: no other firm is allowed to make the medicine
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki cümleler başka firmaların yaptığı jenerik ilaçları anlatıyor; kimse yapamıyorsa 'These' kime işaret edecek?

d.t: Generic medicines must contain exactly the same active ingredient, in the same dose, as the original drug.
d.key: These must contain the same active ingredient in the same amount
d.bait: must contain exactly the same active ingredient
d.why: Bu kural sonraki cümlenin işi. Jeneriklerin NE ZAMAN ve NASIL ortaya çıktığı söylenmeden kuralına geçiliyor; sonraki cümle de aynı şeyi tekrarlamış oluyor.

d.t: Developing a single new drug can take more than ten years and cost billions of dollars.
d.why: Konu ilaç geliştirmenin maliyetine kayıyor; bu önceki cümlede zaten değinilen bir yan nokta. Sonraki 'These' jenerik ilaçları bekliyor.

yol: Önceki cümle 'During this time' ile patent dönemini anlatıyor; sonraki 'These must contain' çoğul bir şeye işaret ediyor ve son cümle 'generics' diyor. Boşluk patentin bittiği anı ve jenerikleri tanıtmalı.

p: Most plants flower every year, but some species of bamboo flower only once every several decades.
What makes them truly remarkable is that all the plants of a species tend to flower at the same moment, wherever they happen to be growing.
This sudden flood of food can cause populations of rats to explode.
Once the seeds have been eaten, the rats turn to stored grain and crops, and in parts of India and Myanmar the result has been famine.
Some scientists think the strategy is a form of defence: by producing far more seeds than animals can eat, the bamboo ensures that at least some survive.
ok: Having flowered and produced an enormous crop of seeds, these plants then die.

kanca.pw: Once the seeds have been eaten

d.t: These rats then breed rapidly, producing several litters within a few months.
d.why: 'These rats' karşılıksız: sıçanlar ancak sonraki cümlede tanıtılıyor.

d.t: Plants of the same species, even on different continents, therefore burst into flower together.
d.key: all the plants of a species tend to flower at the same moment
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Tohumdan hiç söz etmediği için sonraki 'This sudden flood of food' neyin bolluğu olduğunu bulamıyor.

d.t: Some scientists see this as a form of defence against animals that eat seeds.
d.key: the strategy is a form of defence
d.why: Savunma yorumu son cümlenin işi. Tohum ve sıçan zinciri anlatılmadan yoruma geçiliyor; 'this' de henüz anlatılmamış bir stratejiye işaret ediyor.

d.t: In contrast, the plants then produce a vast crop of seeds before dying.
d.key: all the plants of a species tend to flower at the same moment
d.why: İçerik yerinde ama bağlaç yanlış. Tohum vermek aynı anda çiçek açmaya KARŞIT değil, onun devamı; 'In contrast' yanlış bir ilişki kuruyor.

yol: Sonraki cümle 'This sudden flood of food' diyor: boşluk ani bir yiyecek bolluğu tanıtmalı. Önceki cümle hep birlikte çiçeklenmeyi anlattı; doğru cümle çiçekten tohuma geçiyor ('enormous crop of seeds'), dördüncü cümledeki 'the seeds' de buna işaret ediyor.

p: When people with no common language are brought together, for example through trade or forced labour, they often develop a simplified way of communicating.
This kind of language, called a pidgin, has a small vocabulary and very few grammatical rules.
No one speaks a pidgin as a first language; it is used mainly to get practical tasks done, such as buying and selling.
Something remarkable happens, however, when children grow up hearing it.
They do not simply copy the pidgin of their parents but expand it, adding grammatical rules and new words.
ok: Within a generation, it can become a full language with native speakers, known as a creole.

kanca.pw: expand it, adding grammatical rules and new words
No one speaks a pidgin as a first language
when children grow up hearing it

d.t: Many children around the world grow up speaking two or even three different languages at home.
d.bait: two or even three different languages
d.why: Konu çok dilli çocuklara kayıyor. Paragraf pidginin çocukların elinde neye DÖNÜŞTÜĞÜNÜ anlatıyor; dönüşümün sonucu eksik kalıyor.

d.t: As a result, the pidgin usually disappears within a single generation, replaced by the parents' own languages.
d.key: Something remarkable happens
d.why: Yön ters. Paragraf çocukların pidgini GENİŞLETTİĞİNİ ve 'dikkat çekici bir şey' olduğunu söylüyor; pidginin kaybolması bu gidişe ters.

d.t: However, the expanded pidgin becomes a complete language with native speakers, known as a creole.
d.key: expand it, adding grammatical rules and new words
d.why: İçerik yerinde ama bağlaç yanlış. Tam bir dile dönüşmek, genişletmenin SONUCU; ona karşıt değil. 'However' yanlış bir karşıtlık kuruyor.

d.t: Pidgins often borrow most of their words from the language of the more powerful group.
d.key: This kind of language, called a pidgin, has a small vocabulary
d.why: Pidginin söz varlığı ikinci cümlenin yanına, tanıma ait. Sonda yeniden pidgini tanımlamaya dönmek, çocukların başlattığı dönüşümü yarıda bırakıyor.

yol: Paragraf bir dönüşüm anlatıyor: pidgin (kimsenin ana dili değil) → çocuklar onu genişletiyor. Son cümle dönüşümün SONUCUNU vermeli: ana dili olarak konuşulan tam bir dil, yani kreol. 'native speakers' üçüncü cümledeki 'no one speaks it as a first language' ile karşıtlık kuruyor.

p: Sitting with your legs crossed for too long can press on a nerve and the blood vessels that supply it.
Deprived of a proper blood supply, the nerve stops sending normal signals to the brain, and the leg may feel numb.
When you finally move and the pressure is released, the nerve starts working again, but not all at once.
Its fibres send a burst of confused signals as they recover, which the brain experiences as tingling or prickling.
The sensation is usually harmless and fades within a minute or two.
ok: Most people know the strange feeling of a leg that has 'gone to sleep', followed by an uncomfortable prickling.

d.t: This nerve runs down the back of the leg and is the longest in the human body.
d.why: Paragraf 'This nerve' ile açılamaz; sinir ancak sonraki cümlede anılıyor.

d.t: As a result, the leg feels numb and then begins to tingle once you stand up.
d.why: Paragraf 'As a result' ile açılamaz; sonucu olacağı bir sebep önünde yok. Sebep (sinire baskı) ancak sonraki cümlede geliyor.

d.t: Doctors recommend standing up and moving around at least once every hour when working at a desk.
d.why: Odak masa başı çalışma tavsiyesine kayıyor. Paragraf bacağın 'uyuşma' ve 'karıncalanma' mekanizmasını anlatıyor; açılış o deneyimi tanıtmalı.

d.t: A leg that has 'gone to sleep' is actually a sign that blood is flowing to it more strongly than usual.
d.key: Deprived of a proper blood supply
d.why: Yön ters. Üçüncü cümle sinirin kan akışından YOKSUN kaldığını söylüyor; kanın her zamankinden güçlü aktığını söylemek bunu tersine çeviriyor.

yol: Boşluk başta. Paragraf bir deneyimin mekanizmasını adım adım anlatıyor: baskı → uyuşma → baskı kalkınca karıncalanma → zararsız. Açılış bu tanıdık deneyimi tanıtmalı: 'uyuyan' bacak ve ardından gelen karıncalanma.

p: It is often said that a microwave oven cooks food from the inside out, but this is not really true.
The oven produces waves that make water molecules in the food spin back and forth billions of times a second.
In a large piece of food, therefore, the centre is warmed mainly by heat spreading slowly inwards from the outer layers.
This is why instructions often tell you to let a dish stand for a minute or two after cooking, so that the heat can even out.
Stirring halfway through has a similar effect.
ok: This rapid movement creates heat, but the waves can only reach a few centimetres beneath the surface.

kanca.pw: spin back and forth billions of times a second
heat spreading slowly inwards from the outer layers
kanca.ow: only reach a few centimetres beneath the surface

kanca.pw: cooks food from the inside out

d.t: Letting the dish stand for a minute allows the heat to spread evenly through it.
d.key: let a dish stand for a minute or two after cooking
d.why: Bekletme tavsiyesi beşinci cümlenin işi. Isının neden eşit dağılmadığı açıklanmadan çözüme geçiliyor.

d.t: The water molecules inside the food, in short, are set moving extremely quickly by the oven's waves.
d.key: make water molecules in the food spin back and forth
d.bait: set moving extremely quickly by the oven's waves
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Dalgaların ne kadar DERİNE indiğini söylemediği için sonraki 'therefore, the centre is warmed mainly by heat spreading inwards' dayanaksız kalıyor.

d.t: These outer layers then become far hotter than the rest of the dish, sometimes even burning.
d.why: 'These outer layers' karşılıksız: dış katmanlar ancak sonraki cümlede anılıyor. Dalgaların yalnız yüzeye yakın etki ettiği de hiç söylenmemiş oluyor.

d.t: This heat is produced evenly throughout the food, so the centre warms just as fast as the surface.
d.key: the centre is warmed mainly by heat spreading slowly inwards
d.bait: the centre warms just as fast as the surface
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki cümle merkezin, dıştan yavaşça yayılan ısıyla ısındığını söylüyor; ısı her yerde eşit üretilseydi bekletmeye de gerek kalmazdı.

yol: Sonraki cümle 'therefore' ile merkezin DIŞTAN gelen ısıyla ısındığı sonucuna varıyor. Bu sonucun sebebi boşlukta olmalı: dalgalar yalnız birkaç santim derine iner. 'This rapid movement' de önceki cümledeki dönen moleküllere bağlanıyor.

p: In 1972, before President Nixon made historic visits to China and the Soviet Union, the psychologists Baruch Fischhoff and Ruth Beyth asked students to predict how likely various outcomes of the trips were.
After the visits, the same students were asked to recall the predictions they had made.
Knowing the outcome, it seemed, had quietly rewritten their memory of what they had expected.
This hindsight bias, the feeling that we 'knew it all along', can make the past seem far more predictable than it was.
It may also make us judge others' decisions unfairly harshly, once we know how things turned out.
ok: Many of them remembered having given higher odds to the events that had actually happened than they really had.

kanca.ow: the events that had actually happened

d.t: For example, many of them recalled giving higher chances to the events that had in fact taken place.
d.key: asked to recall the predictions they had made
d.why: İçerik yerinde ama bağlaç yanlış. Bu cümle önceki cümlenin bir ÖRNEĞİ değil, deneyin BULGUSU; 'For example' ilişkiyi yanlış kuruyor.

d.t: Nixon's visit to China was the first ever by an American president and changed relations between the two countries for good.
d.bait: changed relations between the two countries
d.why: Konu ziyaretin siyasi önemine kayıyor. Paragraf öğrencilerin belleğini inceliyor; sonraki cümle bir bellek BULGUSU bekliyor.

d.t: Each student, that is, had to remember the probabilities they had written down before the trips.
d.key: the same students were asked to recall the predictions
d.bait: had to remember the probabilities they had written down
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Hatırladıklarının NASIL çarpıldığını söylemediği için sonraki 'rewritten their memory' kanıtsız kalıyor.

d.t: This tendency to believe that we 'knew it all along' is known to psychologists as hindsight bias.
d.key: This hindsight bias, the feeling that we 'knew it all along'
d.bait: is known to psychologists as hindsight bias
d.why: Etkinin adı beşinci cümlenin işi. Bulgu verilmeden ad konuyor; 'This tendency' de henüz gösterilmemiş bir eğilime işaret ediyor.

yol: Önceki cümle 'tahminlerini hatırlamaları istendi' diyor; sonraki 'sonucu bilmek belleklerini yeniden yazmış' diye yorumluyor. Arada BULGU olmalı: gerçekleşen olaylara, aslında verdiklerinden daha yüksek olasılık verdiklerini hatırladılar.

p: Before the 1840s, surgery was a terrifying ordeal, carried out on patients who were fully awake.
Surgeons were valued above all for their speed; some could remove a leg in less than a minute.
Many patients nevertheless died of shock, and many others refused operations altogether, preferring to risk the disease.
In October 1846, at a hospital in Boston, the dentist William Morton gave a patient ether to inhale before a surgeon removed a tumour from his neck.
The patient later reported that he had felt no pain at all.
ok: News of the operation spread within months, and surgeons everywhere began to work without the need for haste.

kanca.pw: valued above all for their speed
removed a tumour from his neck

d.t: This second patient, a young woman, had her leg removed a few weeks later while deeply unconscious.
d.why: 'This second patient' karşılıksız: paragrafta ikinci bir hastadan hiç söz edilmedi.

d.t: Dentists at the time often pulled teeth without any pain relief, and many people suffered from rotten teeth.
d.bait: many people suffered from rotten teeth
d.why: Konu diş sağlığına kayıyor. Morton'un diş hekimi olması yan bilgi; paragraf ameliyatın nasıl DEĞİŞTİĞİNİ anlatıyor ve bunun sonucu eksik kalıyor.

d.t: He had felt nothing at all, he told the doctors, even while the surgeon was cutting deep into his neck.
d.key: he had felt no pain at all
d.bait: He had felt nothing at all
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Bu buluşun cerrahiyi nasıl değiştirdiğini söylemediği için paragrafın başında kurulan 'hız' sorunu çözümsüz kalıyor.

d.t: Most surgeons, however, continued to rely on speed for decades, convinced that ether was too dangerous to use.
d.key: he had felt no pain at all
d.bait: continued to rely on speed for decades
d.why: Yön ters. Paragraf korkunç bir geçmişten bir dönüm noktasına ilerliyor; buluşun onlarca yıl görmezden gelindiğini söylemek bu gidişi tersine çeviriyor.

yol: Paragraf bir 'önce-sonra' hikâyesi: uyanık hasta, HIZ için değer gören cerrahlar → 1846'da eter, acı yok. Son cümle sonucu vermeli: haber yayıldı, cerrahlar artık acele etmeden çalışabildi. 'without the need for haste' ikinci cümledeki 'speed' ile kapanıyor.

p: In 1912 the German meteorologist Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents had once formed a single landmass and had slowly drifted apart over millions of years.
He pointed to the way the coastlines of South America and Africa fit together, and to identical fossils found on both sides of the Atlantic.
It was precisely this gap that most geologists of the day seized on, insisting that no known force could push whole continents through the solid rock of the ocean floor.
Only in the 1960s, when surveys of the seabed revealed that new crust is constantly being formed along mid-ocean ridges, did a mechanism finally appear.
Wegener, who had died on an expedition in Greenland in 1930, did not live to see his theory accepted.
ok: What he could not supply was a convincing account of how anything as massive as a continent could actually move.

kanca.pw: no known force could push whole continents
kanca.ow: how anything as massive as a continent could actually move

d.t: His critics would eventually be proved wrong, and continental drift is now a cornerstone of modern geology.
d.key: did not live to see his theory accepted
d.bait: His critics would eventually be proved wrong
d.why: Zincirde iki halka atlanıyor: önce kuramın zayıf noktası, sonra reddedilişi, en son 1960'larda gelen kanıt. Haklı çıkış paragrafın sonunun işi; burada 'this gap' de karşılıksız kalıyor.

d.t: Therefore, the geologists of his day had little choice but to accept that the continents had once been joined together.
d.key: most geologists of the day seized on
d.why: Önceki cümleye sonuç gibi eklenebilir ama sonraki cümleyle çakışıyor: jeologlar kabul etmedi, kuramın açığına yüklendi. Kanıtlar zorunlu bir sonuç doğurmuyordu; 'Therefore' ilişkiyi yanlış kuruyor.

d.t: He was also able to show exactly which force had pushed the continents slowly across the floor of the ocean.
d.key: no known force could push whole continents
d.bait: able to show exactly which force
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki cümle bilinen bir kuvvet OLMADIĞINI, sondan bir önceki cümle de mekanizmanın ancak 1960'larda bulunduğunu söylüyor.

d.t: The same rock formations and fossil species, he noted, turn up on continents that are now separated by an entire ocean.
d.key: identical fossils found on both sides of the Atlantic
d.bait: turn up on continents that are now separated by an entire ocean
d.why: Önceki cümledeki kanıt listesini yineliyor. Sonraki 'this gap' bir EKSİKLİK bekliyor; kanıt eklemek o eksikliği tanıtmıyor.

yol: Sonraki cümleden başla: 'this gap' (bu açık) bir eksikliğe dönüyor, eleştirmenler de 'hiçbir kuvvet kıtaları itemez' diyor. Boşluk, kanıtları sayan Wegener'in neyi veremediğini söylemeli: kıtaların NASIL hareket ettiğini. Sondan bir önceki cümledeki 'a mechanism finally appear' bunu doğruluyor.

p: Between 1924 and 1932, researchers at the Hawthorne Works, a factory near Chicago, changed the lighting, break times and working hours of small groups of employees.
Almost every change, including a return to the original conditions, seemed to be followed by a rise in output.
The conclusion that many textbooks drew was that the workers were responding not to the changes themselves but to the attention of being studied.
When economists reanalysed the surviving lighting data in 2011, however, they found the famous effect to be far weaker than the legend suggests, and partly explained by seasonal patterns.
The story may therefore say as much about how good tales spread as about how workers behave.
ok: One of the most quoted ideas in social science, that people work harder simply because they are being observed, began in an American factory.

kanca.pw: the Hawthorne Works, a factory near Chicago

kanca.ow: simply because they are being observed
One of the most quoted ideas

d.t: These experiments are still cited in management courses as proof that attention alone can make employees more productive.
d.why: Paragraf 'These experiments' ile açılamaz; deneyler ancak sonraki cümlede anlatılıyor. Ayrıca 'kanıt' diye sunmak, sondaki şüpheyle de çelişiyor.

d.t: Nevertheless, few studies of workplace behaviour have been quoted as often as those carried out in the 1920s.
d.why: Paragraf 'Nevertheless' ile açılamaz; karşı çıkacağı bir önceki söz yok. İçerik açılışa yakın ama bağlaç kapıyı kapatıyor.

d.t: The workers, it was concluded, had been responding to the researchers' attention rather than to the changes in their conditions.
d.key: The conclusion that many textbooks drew
d.why: Sonuç, deneyden önce geliyor. Hangi işçiler, hangi değişiklikler? Bunlar sonraki iki cümlede anlatılıyor; vardığı yargı da dördüncü cümlenin işi.

d.t: Few ideas in social science rest on evidence as solid and as thoroughly tested as the familiar claim that being observed changes how people work.
d.key: far weaker than the legend suggests
d.bait: rest on evidence as solid and as thoroughly tested
d.why: Yön ters. 2011 incelemesi etkinin efsanenin söylediğinden ÇOK DAHA ZAYIF olduğunu buluyor; son cümle hikâyenin yayılışını sorguluyor.

yol: Boşluk başta: paragrafın bütününe bak. Fabrika deneyleri → 'izlendikleri için' çalıştılar yorumu → 2011'de bu yorumun zayıf çıkması → 'iyi hikâyeler nasıl yayılır'. Açılış hem fikri (izlenince daha çok çalışmak) hem yerini (bir Amerikan fabrikası) haber vermeli; 'most quoted' son cümledeki 'how good tales spread' ile kapanıyor.

p: For decades, patients were told to finish every course of antibiotics, even after they felt better, so that surviving bacteria would not develop resistance.
The advice sounds sensible, yet it was never based on strong evidence and was largely a matter of tradition.
Resistance mostly arises when bacteria are exposed to antibiotics, and the longer the exposure, the more opportunities they have to adapt.
Several trials have found that, for some common infections such as certain kinds of pneumonia, shorter courses work just as well as longer ones.
Some experts have therefore argued that the old rule may, in certain cases, encourage the very problem it was meant to prevent.
ok: None of this means patients should simply stop their tablets early; how long a course lasts is for the doctor to decide.

kanca.pw: patients were told to finish every course
kanca.ow: patients should simply stop their tablets early

d.t: Antibiotics, of course, have no effect at all on viruses, such as those that cause colds and most sore throats.
d.bait: have no effect at all on viruses
d.why: Konu virüslere kayıyor. Paragraf antibiyotik KÜRÜNÜN SÜRESİNİ tartışıyor; son cümle bu tartışmayı hasta açısından bağlamalı.

d.t: Taking the drugs for longer than necessary, on this view, could actually help resistant strains of bacteria to survive and spread.
d.key: encourage the very problem it was meant to prevent
d.bait: could actually help resistant strains of bacteria to survive and spread
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor: eski kuralın direnci artırabileceği zaten söylendi. Son cümle bu bulgudan hastanın ne çıkarmalı/çıkarmamalı olduğunu söylemeli.

d.t: Doctors are therefore right to insist that a longer course is always the safer choice, whatever the infection happens to be.
d.key: shorter courses work just as well as longer ones
d.bait: a longer course is always the safer choice
d.why: Yön ters. Paragraf uzun kürün her zaman daha güvenli OLMADIĞINI, kısa kürlerin de işe yaradığını anlatıyor; 'therefore' tam tersi bir sonuca bağlanıyor.

d.t: The second group, by contrast, was given the full two-week course of the same drug, and most of its members recovered more slowly.
d.why: Paragrafta tanıtılmış bir grup yok; 'The second group' neye dönüyor belli değil. Denemeler yalnız genel olarak anılıyor.

yol: Son cümle paragrafı bağlar. Gidiş: eski kural → kanıtı zayıf → kısa kürler de işe yarıyor → kural sorunu artırabilir. Temkinli bir kapanış gerekiyor: 'bu, hastanın ilacı kendi kendine bırakması demek DEĞİL'. 'None of this means' önceki cümledeki iddianın sınırını çiziyor, 'how long a course lasts' kısa/uzun kür tartışmasına dönüyor.

p: Reef-building corals look like rocks, but they are animals, and most of them depend on tiny algae that live inside their tissues.
The algae carry out photosynthesis and pass much of the sugar they produce to their host, which in return offers shelter and nutrients.
Without its partners, the coral loses not only most of its food but also its colour, leaving its white limestone skeleton visible through clear tissue.
A bleached coral is not yet dead, and if temperatures fall again within a few weeks, the algae can return.
When heat waves last longer or come more often, however, many colonies starve before they have a chance to recover.
ok: When the sea stays unusually warm for several weeks, this partnership breaks down and the coral expels the algae from its tissues.

kanca.pw: in return offers shelter and nutrients

d.t: These white skeletons then become easy targets for the storms and burrowing creatures that slowly wear a reef away.
d.key: leaving its white limestone skeleton visible
d.why: 'These white skeletons' henüz anılmadı; beyaz iskelet ancak sonraki cümlede görünür hâle geliyor. Gönderim, karşılığından önce geliyor.

d.t: Coral reefs cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor, yet they are home to about a quarter of all marine species.
d.bait: home to about a quarter of all marine species
d.why: Konu resiflerin biyolojik zenginliğine kayıyor. Sonraki 'Without its partners' bir AYRILIK bekliyor; bu cümle ortaklığın bozulduğunu söylemiyor.

d.t: As a result, the coral turns white and begins to starve, even though it is still very much alive.
d.key: the coral loses not only most of its food but also its colour
d.bait: the coral turns white and begins to starve
d.why: Zincirde halka atlanıyor: sebep (sıcak su, alglerin atılması) söylenmeden sonuca (beyazlama, açlık) geçiliyor. 'As a result' neyin sonucu? Ortaklığın kendisi beyazlatmaz.

d.t: For example, a sudden rise in water temperature can make the coral eject its partners within a matter of days.
d.key: pass much of the sugar they produce to their host
d.why: İçerik boşluğa yakın ama bağlaç yanlış: önceki cümle bir alışverişi anlatıyor, bu cümle o alışverişin ÖRNEĞİ değil, bozulması. Gereken ilişki karşıtlık/dönüm, örnekleme değil.

yol: Sonraki cümle 'Without its partners' diyor: demek ki boşlukta ortaklar ayrılmalı. Önceki cümle ortaklığı (şeker ↔ barınak) kuruyor; boşluk onu bozan olayı vermeli. 'if temperatures fall again' de sebebin SICAKLIK olduğunu doğruluyor.

p: In 1982 two American social scientists, James Q. Wilson and George Kelling, argued that visible signs of disorder, such as broken windows or graffiti, invite more serious crime.
If a neighbourhood looks neglected, they reasoned, potential offenders conclude that nobody is in control.
Supporters often point to New York City, where crime fell sharply in the 1990s after the police began targeting fare-dodging and other minor offences.
Yet crime fell just as steeply in many American cities that never adopted the policy, which makes it hard to say how much of the drop it can claim.
Critics add that aggressive policing of small offences has damaged relations between the police and the communities they serve.
ok: The idea soon moved from academic journals into police departments, which began to treat even minor misbehaviour as a priority.

kanca.ow: The idea soon moved from academic journals

kanca.pw: the police began targeting fare-dodging and other minor offences
kanca.ow: treat even minor misbehaviour as a priority

d.t: Police departments, however, largely ignored the theory and went on concentrating almost entirely on serious and violent crimes.
d.key: the police began targeting fare-dodging and other minor offences
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki cümle polisin küçük suçları HEDEF ALDIĞINI, dördüncü cümle de bunun bir 'policy' olduğunu söylüyor.

d.t: Small signs of neglect, on this view, send the message that the rules in the area are no longer being enforced.
d.key: potential offenders conclude that nobody is in control
d.bait: send the message that the rules in the area are no longer being enforced
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Sonraki cümle bir UYGULAMAYA ('Supporters', 'the police began') geçiyor; kuramın sahaya nasıl taşındığı eksik kalıyor.

d.t: In some cities graffiti has even come to be seen as an art form, with large murals commissioned by local councils.
d.bait: come to be seen as an art form
d.why: Konu grafitinin sanat sayılmasına kayıyor. Paragraf bir suç kuramının polisliğe etkisini izliyor; sonraki cümle buna bağlanmıyor.

d.t: This sharp fall began only after a new mayor took office and promised to restore order to the streets.
d.key: crime fell sharply in the 1990s
d.why: 'This sharp fall' henüz anılmadı; suçtaki düşüş ancak sonraki cümlede geçiyor. Gönderim karşılığından önce geliyor.

yol: Önceki cümle kuramı ('they reasoned') bitiriyor; sonraki cümle 'Supporters' ve polisin küçük suçları hedeflemesiyle bir UYGULAMADAN söz ediyor. Boşluk köprü olmalı: fikir dergilerden polise geçti, küçük suçlar öncelik oldu. Sonraki 'the policy' kelimesi bu köprüyü doğruluyor.

p: A placebo, such as a sugar pill, contains no active ingredient, yet patients who take one often report that their symptoms improve.
For a long time, doctors assumed that this effect depended on deception: the pill could only work if the patient believed it was a real drug.
In 2010, however, a team at Harvard gave patients with irritable bowel syndrome pills that were clearly labelled as placebos, and told them so.
Even though the patients knew they were taking nothing but sugar, many reported greater relief than a group that received no treatment.
Similar results have since been reported for back pain and fatigue, though the studies have mostly been small.
ok: If these findings hold up in larger trials, the ritual of taking a pill may matter more than any deception behind it.

kanca.pw: the studies have mostly been small
kanca.ow: If these findings hold up in larger trials

kanca.pw: the patients knew they were taking nothing but sugar
kanca.ow: the ritual of taking a pill

d.t: The researchers then decided to find out whether a placebo could work without any deception at all.
d.key: pills that were clearly labelled as placebos
d.bait: then decided to find out whether
d.why: Sıra geri gidiyor. Deneyin fikri üçüncü cümleden ÖNCE gelmeliydi; sonuçlar ve benzer çalışmalar anlatıldıktan sonra 'then decided' zinciri bozuyor.

d.t: Therefore, doctors can now safely prescribe sugar pills in place of real drugs for most common conditions.
d.key: the studies have mostly been small
d.why: 'Therefore' bir sonuç çıkarıyor ama önceki cümle tam tersine çalışmaların KÜÇÜK olduğunu söyleyip temkin istiyor. Bu kanıt böyle geniş bir sonuca izin vermez.

d.t: Sugar pills are also widely used in drug trials, so that scientists can compare a new medicine with giving no treatment at all.
d.why: Konu ilaç denemelerindeki kontrol grubuna kayıyor. Paragraf 'aldatma şart mı?' sorusunu izliyor; kapanış bu soruya dönmeli.

d.t: Knowing that a pill is empty, it seems, does not always stop it from making people feel noticeably better.
d.key: Even though the patients knew they were taking nothing but sugar
d.bait: does not always stop it from making people feel noticeably better
d.why: Dördüncü cümlenin bulgusunu yineliyor. Önceki cümle 'çalışmalar küçük' diye bir çekince koydu; son cümle bu çekinceyle birlikte ne anlama geldiğini söylemeli.

yol: Son cümleden önceki çekinceye bak: 'the studies have mostly been small'. Kapanış bu çekinceyi taşımalı (If … hold up in larger trials) ve ikinci cümledeki eski varsayıma (deception) cevap vermeli: önemli olan aldatma değil, hap almanın kendisi olabilir.

p: In 1935 about a hundred cane toads were brought from Hawaii to Queensland in the hope that they would eat the beetles destroying the sugar cane crop.
The toads showed little interest in the beetles, which lived high on the cane stems, out of their reach.
Instead, they ate almost anything else they could catch and, with no natural predators, began to spread across northern Australia.
Their numbers are now estimated in the hundreds of millions, and the poison in their skin kills many native animals that try to eat them, from snakes to quolls.
Few examples show as clearly how a remedy can turn into a problem larger than the one it was meant to solve.
ok: Introducing one species to control another has sometimes worked well, but the history of such schemes also includes some spectacular failures.

kanca.pw: in the hope that they would eat the beetles
kanca.ow: Introducing one species to control another

kanca.pw: a remedy can turn into a problem

d.t: The decision to release them was taken by local sugar growers, who were desperate to save their crops from ruin.
d.why: Paragraf 'them' ile açılamaz; kimin salındığı (kara kurbağaları) ancak sonraki cümlede söyleniyor.

d.t: Few attempts to control a pest with another species have been as successful as the one tried in Australia in the 1930s.
d.key: a remedy can turn into a problem larger than the one it was meant to solve
d.why: Yön ters. Kurbağalar böceklere ilgi göstermedi, yayıldı, yerli hayvanları öldürdü; son cümle de çarenin sorundan büyük bir soruna dönüştüğünü söylüyor.

d.t: The poison in the toads' skin has since killed many of the snakes and quolls that tried to eat them.
d.key: the poison in their skin kills many native animals
d.why: Sonuç, sebepten önce geliyor: kurbağalar getirilmeden, yayılmadan zehirlerinin etkisine geçiliyor. 'has since' (o zamandan beri) henüz anlatılmamış bir olaya dayanıyor; bu bilgi beşinci cümlenin işi.

d.t: As a result, sugar growers in Queensland turned to a natural enemy of the beetles in the 1930s.
d.why: Paragraf 'As a result' ile açılamaz; neyin sonucu olduğu söylenmemiş. İçerik açılışa yakın ama bağlaç bir öncül varsayıyor.

yol: Boşluk başta: son cümleye bak, paragrafın tezi orada: 'çare, sorundan büyük bir sorun oldu'. Açılış bu tezi genel olarak kurmalı: bir türü başkasını kontrol etmek için getirmek bazen işe yarar, bazen felaket olur. Kara kurbağası hikâyesi o genellemenin örneği olarak geliyor.

p: In 1968 the sociologist Robert Merton noticed something odd about the way credit is shared in science.
When a famous researcher and an unknown one publish similar findings, or work together on the same paper, it is usually the famous name that people remember.
Merton called this pattern the Matthew effect, after a line in the Gospel of Matthew: to those who have, more will be given.
The advantage tends to build on itself, since well-known scientists find it easier to win grants, attract talented students and publish in prestigious journals.
Small differences in reputation early in a career can thus grow into very large differences in influence later on.
ok: The lesser-known colleague, meanwhile, often receives little or no recognition, even for a contribution that was every bit as important.

kanca.pw: it is usually the famous name that people remember
to those who have, more will be given

d.t: Merton himself had changed his name as a teenager, from Meyer Schkolnick, while he was performing as an amateur stage magician.
d.bait: performing as an amateur stage magician
d.why: Konu Merton'ın hayatına kayıyor. Sonraki 'this pattern' bir örüntüye dönmeli; isim değiştirme hikâyesi bir örüntü değil.

d.t: Readers and other scientists, in such cases, tend to recall the better-known author and forget the less familiar one entirely.
d.key: it is usually the famous name that people remember
d.bait: tend to recall the better-known author
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Sonraki alıntı ('sahip olana daha çok verilir') madalyonun öbür yüzünü, yani tanınmayanın KAYBINI bekliyor; bu cümle yeni bir şey eklemiyor.

d.t: This line, written almost two thousand years earlier, seemed to him to describe the situation in science perfectly.
d.key: after a line in the Gospel of Matthew
d.why: 'This line' henüz anılmadı; İncil'deki satır ancak sonraki cümlede veriliyor. Gönderim karşılığından önce geliyor.

d.t: Over time, however, such imbalances usually disappear, as the real contribution of each author gradually comes to light and is rewarded.
d.key: The advantage tends to build on itself
d.why: Yön ters. Paragraf dengesizliğin zamanla BÜYÜDÜĞÜNÜ söylüyor ('build on itself', 'very large differences').

yol: Önceki cümle ünlü ismin hatırlandığını söylüyor; sonraki cümle buna 'sahip olana daha çok verilir' örüntüsü diyor. Örüntünün tamamlanması için öbür yüz gerekli: tanınmayan araştırmacı, eşit katkısına rağmen görünmez kalıyor. 'an unknown one' → 'The lesser-known colleague' gönderimi yolu gösteriyor.

p: In 1989 the epidemiologist David Strachan noticed that children with many older siblings were less likely to develop hay fever.
He suggested that infections passed around in large families might train the immune system, and the idea became known as the hygiene hypothesis.
It was widely taken to mean that modern homes were simply too clean and that children needed more exposure to germs.
Later research, however, has shown that common childhood infections such as measles offer little or no protection against allergies.

Many scientists now favour the 'old friends' explanation, which holds that what matters is contact with the harmless microbes found in soil, animals and the human gut, with which our immune systems evolved.
ok: On this view, cutting back on household cleaning would do little good, whereas time outdoors and a varied diet might.

kanca.pw: modern homes were simply too clean
kanca.ow: cutting back on household cleaning would do little good

kanca.pw: soil, animals and the human gut
kanca.ow: time outdoors and a varied diet

d.t: Researchers therefore began to ask whether fewer infections in small families could explain the rise in allergies.
d.key: He suggested that infections passed around in large families
d.why: Sıra geri gidiyor: bu soru Strachan'ın 1989'daki adımı, ikinci cümlede zaten atıldı. Yeni açıklamaya geçtikten sonra eski soruya dönmek zinciri bozuyor.

d.t: Hay fever occurs when the immune system overreacts to pollen from grasses, trees and weeds, usually in spring and summer.
d.why: Konu saman nezlesinin tanımına kayıyor. Paragraf 'ev fazla mı temiz?' yorumunun yerini neyin aldığını anlatıyor; kapanış bunun pratik sonucunu söylemeli.

d.t: According to this account, the key is regular contact with harmless microbes rather than with the germs that actually cause illness.
d.key: contact with the harmless microbes
d.bait: the key is regular contact with harmless microbes
d.why: Önceki cümleyi başka sözlerle yineliyor. Üçüncü cümledeki 'evler fazla temiz' yorumu hâlâ cevapsız; kapanış eski yorumla yeni açıklamayı karşılaştırmalı.

d.t: Even so, these microbes are thought to teach the immune system not to overreact to harmless substances such as pollen.
d.key: Many scientists now favour the 'old friends' explanation
d.why: 'Even so' (yine de) bir karşı çıkış bekler, ama önceki cümle bu mikropları zaten destekliyor; bu cümle o açıklamayı sürdürüyor, ona rağmen bir şey söylemiyor.

yol: Paragraf iki açıklamayı yarıştırıyor: 'evler fazla temiz, mikrop lazım' ↔ 'zararsız eski dostlar lazım'. Son cümle bunun pratik sonucunu vermeli. 'On this view' önceki açıklamaya bağlanıyor; 'household cleaning' üçüncü cümleye, 'time outdoors and a varied diet' toprak ve bağırsak mikroplarına dönüyor.

p: In 1985 British scientists in Antarctica reported that the ozone layer above them was becoming dramatically thinner each spring.
The ozone layer absorbs most of the sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation, so its loss raised fears of more skin cancers and damaged crops.
These chemicals, released from fridges, air conditioners and aerosol cans, drift high into the atmosphere, where sunlight breaks them apart and frees chlorine atoms that destroy ozone.
Within two years, governments signed the Montreal Protocol, agreeing to phase out their production.
Recent measurements suggest that the layer is slowly healing, although a full recovery over Antarctica is not expected before the 2060s.
ok: The main culprit turned out to be a family of human-made gases, chlorofluorocarbons, that had once been praised as perfectly safe.

d.t: This agreement was later strengthened several times as scientists learned more about the scale of the damage.
d.key: governments signed the Montreal Protocol
d.why: 'This agreement' henüz anılmadı; Montreal Protokolü iki cümle sonra geliyor. Sonraki 'These chemicals' de karşılıksız kalıyor.

d.t: Natural processes, rather than human activity, were soon shown to be responsible for most of the thinning over the pole.
d.key: released from fridges, air conditioners and aerosol cans
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki cümle suçluyu buzdolabı, klima ve spreylerden çıkan İNSAN YAPIMI kimyasallar olarak gösteriyor.

d.t: Ultraviolet light is also what allows the skin to make vitamin D, which the body needs in order to keep its bones strong.
d.bait: allows the skin to make vitamin D
d.why: Konu D vitaminine kayıyor. Paragraf incelmenin SEBEBİNİ ve çözümünü izliyor; sonraki 'These chemicals' bir kimyasal bekliyor.

d.t: Governments quickly agreed to ban the gases responsible, and the layer has since shown clear signs of beginning to recover.
d.key: Recent measurements suggest that the layer is slowly healing
d.bait: Governments quickly agreed to ban the gases responsible
d.why: Zincirde halka atlanıyor: sebep açıklanmadan çözüme ve iyileşmeye geçiliyor. Yasak dördüncü, iyileşme son cümlenin işi; sonraki cümle ise hâlâ kimyasalların nasıl zarar verdiğini anlatıyor.

yol: Sonraki cümle 'These chemicals' ile başlıyor: boşlukta kimyasallar TANITILMALI. Önceki cümle kaybın sonuçlarını (cilt kanseri, ürün) söyledi; doğal soru 'sebebi ne?'. Boşluk suçluyu (CFC'ler) vermeli; protokolün 'their production' ifadesi de insan yapımı gazlara dönüyor.

p: In 1902 the French colonial government in Hanoi, alarmed by the rats spreading through the city's new sewers, offered residents a small reward for every rat they killed.
To spare officials the unpleasant task of counting bodies, hunters only had to hand in the tail.
Before long, rats without tails were spotted running through the streets, released by hunters who wanted them to go on breeding.
Some enterprising residents were even reported to be raising rats on farms outside the city purely for the bounty.
Economists now use the episode to illustrate a familiar problem: once a measure becomes a target, people find ways to hit the target without achieving the goal.
ok: Thousands of tails soon arrived every day, yet the city seemed to have just as many rats as ever.

kanca.pw: hunters only had to hand in the tail

kanca.ow: the city seemed to have just as many rats as ever

kanca.pw: hit the target without achieving the goal
kanca.ow: yet the city seemed to have just as many rats

d.t: These farms were eventually discovered by the authorities, and the reward was quietly cancelled soon afterwards.
d.key: raising rats on farms outside the city
d.why: 'These farms' henüz anılmadı; çiftlikler ancak iki cümle sonra geliyor. Gönderim karşılığından önce düşüyor.

d.t: Rats also carry the fleas that spread plague, a disease that reached Hanoi only a year or so later.
d.why: Konu vebaya kayıyor. Paragraf ödül sisteminin nasıl ters teptiğini anlatıyor; sonraki cümle kuyruksuz fareleri bir BİLMECENİN cevabı olarak getiriyor.

d.t: The number of rats in the city fell quickly, and within a few months the sewers were said to be almost empty.
d.key: rats without tails were spotted running through the streets
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki cümleler avcıların fareleri ÜRETMEYE devam ettirdiğini anlatıyor; son cümle de hedefe ulaşılıp amacın kaçırıldığını söylüyor.

d.t: A tail, rather than a whole dead animal, was all that a hunter needed to show to collect the reward.
d.key: hunters only had to hand in the tail
d.bait: was all that a hunter needed to show
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Sonraki cümle kuyruksuz fareleri bir açıklama gibi sunuyor; önce bir tuhaflık (kuyruk çok, fare azalmıyor) söylenmeli.

yol: Sonraki cümle 'kuyruksuz fareler görüldü' diyor: bu, bir bilmecenin cevabı. Boşluk o bilmeceyi kurmalı: kuyruklar yağıyor ama fareler azalmıyor. Önceki cümledeki 'hand in the tail' kuyruk sayısına, son cümledeki 'hit the target without achieving the goal' bu çelişkiye bağlanıyor.

p: In the 1840s, the Vienna General Hospital had two maternity wards, and in one of them women were dying of childbirth fever at several times the rate of the other.
The first ward was staffed by doctors and medical students, who often came straight from performing autopsies, while the second was run by midwives.
Semmelweis concluded that the doctors were carrying something from the corpses on their hands and, in 1847, ordered them to wash in a chlorine solution.

Deaths in the first ward fell dramatically, yet many senior physicians, offended by the suggestion that they themselves were spreading disease, refused to accept his findings, and his career in Vienna soon came to an end.
ok: Today it seems obvious that doctors should wash their hands, but Ignaz Semmelweis paid a high price for saying so.

kanca.pw: his career in Vienna soon came to an end
kanca.ow: paid a high price for saying so

d.t: However, doctors in the mid-nineteenth century rarely washed their hands, even between one patient and the next.
d.why: Paragraf 'However' ile açılamaz; karşı çıkacağı bir önceki söz yok. Ayrıca dördüncü cümlede soyadıyla anılan Semmelweis hiç tanıtılmamış oluyor.

d.t: Once the doctors began washing in chlorine, deaths in their ward dropped to the level of the midwives' ward.
d.key: Deaths in the first ward fell dramatically
d.bait: Once the doctors began washing in chlorine
d.why: Sonuç en başa konuyor: hangi doktorlar, hangi koğuş, neden klor? Sorun ikinci cümlede, çözüm dördüncüde, sonuç beşincide geliyor.

d.t: Few medical discoveries were welcomed as warmly by the doctors of their day as the simple importance of keeping hands clean.
d.key: refused to accept his findings
d.why: Yön ters. Son cümle kıdemli hekimlerin bulguyu REDDETTİĞİNİ ve Semmelweis'in kariyerinin bittiğini söylüyor.

d.t: This difference puzzled a young assistant doctor who had only recently joined the staff of the hospital.
d.why: Paragraf 'This difference' ile açılamaz; iki koğuş arasındaki fark ancak sonraki cümlede veriliyor.

yol: Boşluk başta. Dördüncü cümle 'Semmelweis' diye soyadıyla başlıyor: demek ki ondan önce tam adıyla tanıtılmış olmalı. Son cümle kariyerinin bittiğini söylüyor. Açılış hem kişiyi hem bedeli (paid a high price) haber veriyor; 'should wash their hands' de klorlu suyla yıkama emrine bağlanıyor.

p: Each autumn, millions of monarch butterflies leave Canada and the northern United States and fly as far as 4,000 kilometres to a few mountain forests in central Mexico.
They spend the winter there, clustered on fir trees in such numbers that the branches sometimes bend under their weight.
No single butterfly makes the whole round trip; the journey north is completed by their children, grandchildren and even great-grandchildren.
How the autumn generation finds forests that none of its ancestors from the previous year has ever seen remains one of the most puzzling questions in animal navigation.
Experiments suggest that the butterflies use the sun as a compass, correcting for its movement across the sky with an internal clock in their antennae.
ok: In spring they head north again, but they lay their eggs along the way and die long before reaching Canada.

kanca.ow: In spring they head north again

kanca.pw: No single butterfly makes the whole round trip

d.t: The forests are now officially protected, although illegal logging has steadily reduced the area available to the butterflies.
d.why: Konu ormanların korunmasına kayıyor. Sonraki cümle 'kimse gidiş-dönüşün tamamını yapmıyor' diyor; önce kuzeye dönüş yolculuğu başlamalı.

d.t: The sun, it appears, serves them as a compass, adjusted throughout the day by a clock in their antennae.
d.key: use the sun as a compass
d.why: Cevap sorudan önce geliyor. Yön bulma bilmecesi beşinci cümlede soruluyor, güneş pusulası son cümlede cevaplanıyor; burada zincir atlanıyor.

d.t: Even so, a single winter storm in the mountains can kill millions of them in one night.
d.key: clustered on fir trees in such numbers
d.why: 'Even so' (yine de) bir güvenceye karşı çıkar; önceki cümlede öyle bir güvence yok. Sonraki cümle de fırtınaya değil, kuzeye dönüş yolculuğuna bağlanıyor.

d.t: Huge numbers of them gather on the very same trees, covering the branches so densely that they hang down under the load.
d.key: the branches sometimes bend under their weight
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Sonraki cümlenin 'journey north' ve 'their children' ifadeleri bir dönüş yolculuğu ve yumurtlama bekliyor.

yol: Sonraki cümle iki şey bekliyor: kuzeye bir yolculuk ('the journey north') ve yeni nesiller ('their children'). Önceki cümle kışı anlatıyor. Boşluk ilkbaharda kuzeye dönüşü, yolda yumurtlamayı ve kelebeklerin Kanada'ya varmadan ölmesini vermeli.

p: In 1964 a New York newspaper reported that thirty-eight neighbours had watched Kitty Genovese being attacked outside her home and that none of them had called the police.
The story shocked the nation and inspired a famous line of research into what psychologists named the bystander effect: the larger the crowd, the less likely any individual is to help.
Later investigations, however, found that the newspaper had exaggerated; few of the neighbours saw the attack clearly, and at least one did call for help.
More recently, a 2019 study analysed security-camera footage of real public conflicts in three countries.
In about nine out of ten cases, at least one bystander stepped in, and the more people were present, the more likely it was that someone would.
ok: Crowds in real life, it seems, are far less indifferent than the famous story once led people to believe.

kanca.pw: the more people were present, the more likely
none of them had called the police

kanca.ow: the famous story once led people to believe

d.t: Large crowds, these findings confirm, make each individual noticeably less willing to get involved when trouble starts.
d.key: the more people were present, the more likely it was that someone would
d.bait: make each individual noticeably less willing
d.why: Yön ters. Önceki cümle kalabalık büyüdükçe birinin müdahale etme ihtimalinin ARTTIĞINI söylüyor; 'confirm' tam tersini doğruluyormuş gibi yapıyor.

d.t: Such cameras have also raised serious concerns about privacy in many of the cities where they have been installed in large numbers.
d.key: security-camera footage
d.why: Konu kameraların mahremiyet sorununa kayıyor. Paragraf seyirci etkisi efsanesinin sorgulanmasını anlatıyor; kapanış o sonuca varmalı.

d.t: These neighbours, the researchers concluded, would almost certainly have acted differently if each had been alone that night.
d.key: thirty-eight neighbours
