yol: Sonraki cümledeki 'however' ve 'much weaker' bir şeyi küçültüyor: demek ki önce bulgu BÜYÜTÜLMÜŞ olmalı. Boşluk o büyütmeyi vermeli: ebeveynlik kitapları öz denetimi başarının anahtarı saydı. Dördüncü cümledeki 'predicted little about later achievement' bu 'key to later success' iddiasını çürütüyor.

p: On long voyages, sailors' gums would swell and bleed, old wounds would reopen, and many men died long before reaching their destination.
In 1747 the Scottish naval surgeon James Lind divided twelve sick sailors into pairs and gave each pair a different remedy, from cider and vinegar to seawater.
The two men who received oranges and lemons recovered so quickly that one of them was soon fit for duty.
Surprisingly, it took the British navy almost fifty years to begin issuing lemon juice to all its crews.
Lind himself seems not to have grasped how important his result was, and he went on recommending other treatments as well.
ok: For centuries, scurvy was among the most feared diseases at sea, thought to have killed more sailors than battles did.

kanca.pw: sailors' gums would swell and bleed

d.t: Scurvy was usually a mild complaint at sea, rarely troubling sailors for more than a few uncomfortable days.
d.key: many men died long before reaching their destination
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki cümle diş etlerinin kanadığını, yaraların açıldığını ve pek çok denizcinin öldüğünü söylüyor.

d.t: Lemon juice became a standard part of every British sailor's rations at the end of the eighteenth century.
d.key: issuing lemon juice to all its crews
d.why: Hikâyenin sonu başa konuyor: hastalık ve Lind'in deneyi anlatılmadan çözüme geçiliyor. Bu bilgi beşinci cümlenin işi.

d.t: Nevertheless, the doctors of the time had very little idea of what caused the disease or how it might be treated.
d.why: Paragraf 'Nevertheless' ile açılamaz; karşı çıkacağı bir önceki söz yok. 'the disease' de hiç adlandırılmadı.

d.t: Sailors on long voyages often suffered from bleeding gums, aching joints and wounds that simply would not heal.
d.key: sailors' gums would swell and bleed
d.bait: bleeding gums, aching joints and wounds that simply would not heal
d.why: Sonraki cümle aynı belirtileri zaten veriyor; açılış onu önden tekrar ediyor. Hastalığın adı (iskorbüt) da hiç konmuyor.

yol: Boşluk başta. Sonraki cümle bir hastalığın belirtilerini adını vermeden sayıyor: demek ki ad ve önem açılışta konmalı. Açılış hastalığı (scurvy) adlandırıyor ve denizdeki ağırlığını veriyor; 'many men died' cümlesi bunu somutlaştırıyor.

p: Why is the sky dark at night?
The question sounds childish, but if the universe were infinitely large, unchanging and evenly filled with stars, every line of sight should end on the surface of a star.
This puzzle, now called Olbers' paradox after a German astronomer who described it in 1823, troubled scientists for more than a century.
Its solution lies in two facts that were unknown at the time: the universe has a finite age, and it is expanding.
Light from the most distant stars has simply not had time to reach us, and the light that does arrive is stretched towards wavelengths our eyes cannot see.
ok: The night sky would then blaze like the surface of the sun, yet in reality it is almost completely black.

kanca.pw: every line of sight should end on the surface of a star
kanca.ow: blaze like the surface of the sun
yet in reality it is almost completely black

kanca.pw: Why is the sky dark at night?

d.t: These two facts were discovered only in the twentieth century, long after the astronomer himself had died.
d.key: two facts that were unknown at the time
d.why: 'These two facts' henüz anılmadı; iki gerçek ancak beşinci cümlede veriliyor. Gönderim karşılığından önce düşüyor.

d.t: Stars differ widely in colour and size, from cool red dwarfs to hot blue giants many times larger than the sun.
d.bait: from cool red dwarfs to hot blue giants
d.why: Konu yıldız türlerine kayıyor. Sonraki 'This puzzle' bir BİLMECE bekliyor; bu cümle beklenti ile gerçek arasındaki çelişkiyi kurmuyor.

d.t: The sky would then appear even darker than it does, since the stars would block one another's light.
d.key: every line of sight should end on the surface of a star
d.why: Yön ters. Her bakış çizgisi bir yıldızda bitiyorsa gökyüzü KARANLIK değil, parlak olmalı; çelişki de buradan doğuyor.

d.t: For example, the nearest star beyond the sun lies more than four light years away from the Earth.
d.key: every line of sight should end on the surface of a star
d.why: 'For example' önceki cümleye bağlanmıyor: en yakın yıldızın uzaklığı, sonsuz evren varsayımının örneği değil. Sonraki 'This puzzle' de bir bilmece bulamıyor.

yol: Sonraki cümle 'This puzzle' diyor: boşlukta bir ÇELİŞKİ kurulmalı. Önceki cümle bir beklenti veriyor (her bakış bir yıldıza çıkar); boşluk bunun sonucunu (gökyüzü güneş gibi parlamalı) ve gerçeği (ama kapkara) yan yana koymalı. İlk cümledeki soru da 'black' ile kapanıyor.

p: In a well-known study from 1974, Elizabeth Loftus and John Palmer showed people a film of a car accident and then asked them how fast the cars had been going.
The only difference between the groups was a single verb: the cars had 'hit', 'collided with' or 'smashed into' each other.
Those who heard 'smashed' gave the highest estimates of speed.
A week later, they were also more than twice as likely to say that they had seen broken glass, although there had been none in the film.
The wording of the question, it seems, had not only shaped their answers but quietly rewritten the memory itself.
ok: For courts, the lesson is uncomfortable: the way a witness is questioned can change what the witness remembers.

kanca.ow: the way a witness is questioned

d.t: A single word in a question, on this evidence, is enough to alter what people believe they saw.
d.key: quietly rewritten the memory itself
d.bait: is enough to alter what people believe they saw
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Paragraf bulguyu zaten özetledi; kapanış bu bulgunun dışarıdaki SONUCUNU (tanık ifadeleri) söylemeli.

d.t: The researchers then asked whether a leading question could also add details that had never been there.
d.key: they were also more than twice as likely to say that they had seen broken glass
d.why: Sıra geri gidiyor: bu soru kırık cam bulgusundan ÖNCE sorulmalıydı. Cevap dördüncü cümlede zaten verildi.

d.t: Memories of dramatic events, the study confirmed, stay accurate however the questions about them happen to be worded.
d.key: had not only shaped their answers
d.bait: stay accurate however the questions about them happen to be worded
d.why: Yön ters. Paragraf soru kelimesinin cevapları VE anıyı değiştirdiğini gösteriyor; olmayan kırık camı 'görenler' bunun kanıtı.

d.t: Car accidents remain one of the leading causes of death among young adults in many countries around the world.
d.bait: leading causes of death among young adults
d.why: Konu trafik kazalarına kayıyor. Deneydeki kaza yalnız bir araç; paragraf hafızanın sorularla değişmesini anlatıyor.

yol: Paragraf bir deneyden genel bir ilkeye çıkıyor: soru kelimesi → hız tahmini → olmayan kırık cam → anı yeniden yazıldı. Kapanış ilkeyi gerçek hayata taşımalı: tanığın nasıl sorgulandığı, ne hatırladığını değiştirebilir. 'The wording of the question' ile 'the way a witness is questioned' örtüşüyor.

p: Carbon monoxide is sometimes called the silent killer, because it has no colour, smell or taste.
It is produced whenever fuel such as gas, oil, wood or coal burns without enough oxygen, for example in a faulty boiler or a blocked chimney.
As a result, the blood carries less and less oxygen, even though the victim may be breathing normally.
The early symptoms, such as headache, dizziness and tiredness, are easily mistaken for flu, which is one reason the danger often goes unnoticed until it is too late.
An inexpensive alarm fitted near any fuel-burning appliance is therefore one of the simplest ways of protecting a household.
ok: Once inhaled, the gas binds to the haemoglobin in red blood cells far more tightly than oxygen does, taking its place.

kanca.pw: the blood carries less and less oxygen

d.t: For this reason, gas boilers and other fuel-burning appliances should be checked every year by a qualified engineer.
d.key: As a result, the blood carries less and less oxygen
d.why: Önceki cümleye uyuyor ama sonrakini kopartıyor: 'As a result, the blood carries less oxygen' kazan bakımının sonucu olamaz. Neden-sonuç zinciri gazın vücutta ne yaptığına bağlanmalı.

d.t: These symptoms tend to improve when the person leaves the house for a while, which can be a useful clue.
d.key: The early symptoms, such as headache, dizziness and tiredness
d.why: 'These symptoms' henüz anılmadı; belirtiler ancak iki cümle sonra sayılıyor. Gönderim karşılığından önce düşüyor.

d.t: Because it cannot be seen or smelled, people usually have no idea at all that they are breathing it in.
d.key: it has no colour, smell or taste
d.why: İlk cümleyi yineliyor. Sonraki 'As a result, the blood carries less oxygen' gazın KANDA ne yaptığını bekliyor; bu cümle o halkayı vermiyor.

d.t: Fitting an alarm near boilers, stoves and open fires is the simplest way of keeping a whole family safe from the gas.
d.key: An inexpensive alarm fitted near any fuel-burning appliance
d.why: Çözüm, mekanizmadan önce geliyor: gazın nasıl öldürdüğü anlatılmadan alarma geçiliyor. Bu son cümlenin işi; sonraki 'As a result' de dayanaksız kalıyor.

yol: Sonraki cümle 'As a result, the blood carries less and less oxygen' diyor: boşluk kandaki oksijeni azaltan SEBEBİ vermeli. Önceki cümle gazın nerede oluştuğunu söyledi; boşluk solunduktan sonra ne yaptığını anlatmalı: hemoglobine oksijenden sıkı bağlanıp onun yerini alıyor.

p: These animals, rarely more than a millimetre long, live in moss, soil and lake beds almost everywhere on Earth, from mountain tops to the deep sea.
When their surroundings dry out, they pull in their legs, lose almost all of their water and shrivel into a dormant state known as a tun.
In this condition their metabolism slows to less than a hundredth of its normal rate, and they can survive freezing, intense radiation and even, in one experiment, the vacuum of space.
Added water can bring them back to life within hours, sometimes after years of apparent death.
Researchers hope that understanding how they protect their cells could one day help to preserve vaccines without refrigeration.
ok: Tardigrades, often called water bears, are thought to be among the toughest animals on the planet, despite their tiny size.

kanca.pw: rarely more than a millimetre long
they can survive freezing, intense radiation
kanca.ow: among the toughest animals on the planet

d.t: Their remarkable resistance to drying out was first described by an Italian scientist in the eighteenth century.
d.why: Paragraf 'Their' ile açılamaz; kimin direnci? Hayvan henüz adlandırılmadı. Sonraki 'These animals' de bu cümlede bir hayvan bulamıyor.

d.t: However, some of the smallest creatures on Earth turn out to be among the very hardiest that scientists have ever studied.
d.why: Paragraf 'However' ile açılamaz; karşı çıkacağı bir önceki söz yok. İçerik açılışa yakın ama bağlaç bir öncül varsayıyor.

d.t: Once rehydrated, these tiny creatures simply crawl away and carry on with their lives as if nothing had happened.
d.key: Added water can bring them back to life
d.why: Sonuç başa konuyor: kurumadan, uyku hâlinden söz edilmeden 'yeniden suyla dolunca' deniyor. Bu adım beşinci cümlenin işi.

d.t: Tardigrades are delicate creatures that can survive only in a narrow range of damp, mild and stable conditions.
d.key: they can survive freezing, intense radiation
d.bait: delicate creatures that can survive only in a narrow range
d.why: Yön ters. Paragraf donmaya, radyasyona, hatta uzay boşluğuna dayanabildiklerini anlatıyor; 'narrow range' bunun tam tersi.

yol: Boşluk başta. Sonraki cümle 'These animals' diyor: açılışta hayvan ADIYLA tanıtılmalı. Paragrafın geri kalanı bir dayanıklılık listesi (kuruma, donma, radyasyon, uzay); açılış bu tezi kurmalı. 'rarely more than a millimetre long' ise 'despite their tiny size' ile örtüşüyor.

p: In 1887 Ludwik Zamenhof, an eye doctor in a part of the Russian Empire where Poles, Jews, Germans and Russians lived side by side, published a book introducing a new language called Esperanto.
He believed that much of the hostility he saw around him came from people being unable to understand one another.
Its grammar has no irregular verbs, and its vocabulary is drawn mainly from European languages, so speakers of those languages can learn it remarkably quickly.

Yet despite more than a century of enthusiasm, Esperanto has never come close to becoming the world's second language; estimates of fluent speakers range from tens of thousands to perhaps two million.
ok: His answer was a neutral language that belonged to no nation and that anyone could learn within months.

kanca.pw: people being unable to understand one another

d.t: Eye diseases were common in the crowded towns of the region, and he treated many poor patients for free.
d.key: an eye doctor
d.bait: treated many poor patients for free
d.why: Konu Zamenhof'un hekimliğine kayıyor. Önceki cümle bir sorun koydu (anlaşamamak); sonraki 'Its grammar' bir dilin tanıtılmasını bekliyor.

d.t: Misunderstanding between the different communities, he was convinced, lay at the root of much of their mutual distrust.
d.key: hostility he saw around him came from people being unable to understand one another
d.bait: lay at the root of much of their mutual distrust
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Sorun zaten kondu; şimdi ÇÖZÜM gelmeli ki sonraki 'Its grammar' bir dile bağlanabilsin.

d.t: Nevertheless, he spent several years testing his invented language by translating poems and plays into it himself.
d.key: He believed that much of the hostility
d.why: 'Nevertheless' (yine de) bir karşıtlık bekler; önceki cümledeki inançla dil geliştirmesi arasında karşıtlık yok, tam tersine biri ötekinin sebebi. Dilin neden 'tarafsız' ve kolay olması gerektiği de söylenmiyor.

d.t: These learners usually reach a basic level of fluency in about a quarter of the time needed for French.
d.why: 'These learners' karşılıksız; paragrafta henüz öğrenen kimse yok, dilin yapısı bile anlatılmadı.

yol: Önceki cümle bir SORUN veriyor: insanlar birbirini anlamadığı için düşmanlık var. Sonraki cümle 'Its grammar' ile bir dili anlatıyor. Boşluk köprü: sorunun çözümü olarak tarafsız, kolay öğrenilen bir dil. 'anyone could learn within months' sonraki 'remarkably quickly' ile örtüşüyor.

p: Students who stay up all night before an exam often assume that every extra hour of study can only help.
Research on sleep suggests otherwise.
During deep sleep, the brain appears to replay the day's experiences, transferring new memories from the hippocampus, a temporary store, to the cortex, where they can be kept for the long term.
In experiments, people who slept after learning a list of word pairs remembered noticeably more of them the next day than people who stayed awake for the same length of time.
Sleep also seems to help the brain spot hidden patterns in what it has learned, which may explain why solutions sometimes appear after a good night's rest.
ok: Giving up a night's sleep in order to study more may therefore cost a student more than it gains.

kanca.pw: Students who stay up all night
kanca.ow: Giving up a night's sleep in order to study more

kanca.pw: every extra hour of study can only help
kanca.ow: cost a student more than it gains

d.t: Caffeine, which many students rely on during exams, can stay in the body for several hours after the last cup.
d.bait: can stay in the body for several hours
d.why: Konu kafeine kayıyor. Paragraf ilk cümledeki varsayımı (her ekstra saat işe yarar) çürütüyor; kapanış o varsayıma dönmeli.

d.t: A rested brain, it appears, is better at noticing hidden patterns and finding answers to difficult problems.
d.key: help the brain spot hidden patterns
d.bait: is better at noticing hidden patterns
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Kanıtlar sıralandı; kapanış bunları baştaki öğrenciye bağlamalı.

d.t: Staying awake to revise is therefore the most reliable way to fix new information firmly in memory.
d.key: people who slept after learning a list of word pairs remembered noticeably more
d.bait: the most reliable way to fix new information
d.why: Yön ters. Deneyde uyuyanlar uyanık kalanlardan DAHA ÇOK hatırladı; 'therefore' tam tersi bir sonuca bağlanıyor.

d.t: Scientists therefore set out to test whether people remember more after a night's sleep than after staying awake.
d.key: people who slept after learning a list of word pairs
d.why: Sıra geri gidiyor: bu deney dördüncü cümlede zaten yapıldı ve sonucu verildi. Sonuçtan sonra 'test etmeye koyuldular' zinciri bozuyor.

yol: Paragraf bir varsayımla açılıyor (her ekstra çalışma saati işe yarar), 'otherwise' ile çürütüyor ve üç kanıt veriyor. Kapanış çemberi kapatmalı: uykudan vazgeçmek kazandırdığından fazlasını kaybettirebilir. 'Giving up a night's sleep' ilk cümledeki 'stay up all night' kalıbına dönüyor.

p: According to a popular saying, lightning never strikes the same place twice.
The physics of a thunderstorm, however, gives no reason to believe it, and the evidence points firmly the other way.
Tall, isolated structures such as towers, masts and lone trees are especially likely targets, which is why the Empire State Building in New York is hit around twenty times a year.
Even people can be struck more than once: a US park ranger, Roy Sullivan, survived seven separate lightning strikes between 1942 and 1977.
The saying, in short, may be useful as a figure of speech, but as a safety rule it is dangerously wrong.
ok: Lightning follows the easiest path to the ground, and a spot that offered one before will usually offer it again.

kanca.ow: Lightning follows the easiest path to the ground
the easiest path to the ground

d.t: These seven strikes left him with burns on his body and, on one occasion, without his eyebrows.
d.key: survived seven separate lightning strikes
d.why: 'These seven strikes' henüz anılmadı; yedi yıldırım ve 'him' (Roy Sullivan) ancak iki cümle sonra geliyor.

d.t: For example, a single flash of lightning can heat the surrounding air to temperatures hotter than the surface of the sun.
d.key: gives no reason to believe it
d.why: 'For example' önceki cümleye bağlanmıyor: havanın ısınması, 'aynı yere iki kez düşmez' inancının neden yanlış olduğuna örnek değil. Sonraki cümle de yüksek yapılara geçiyor.

d.t: Thunder, by contrast, is simply the sound of air expanding violently as it is heated by the flash.
d.bait: the sound of air expanding violently
d.why: Konu gök gürültüsüne kayıyor. Paragraf yıldırımın NEREYE düştüğünü tartışıyor; sonraki cümle hedef seçimine devam ediyor.

d.t: Scientists, in fact, see nothing at all in the way storms behave that would support the old belief.
d.key: gives no reason to believe it
d.bait: see nothing at all in the way storms behave
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. İnancın neden yanlış olduğu, yani yıldırımın nasıl yol seçtiği söylenmeden sonraki 'especially likely targets' havada kalıyor.

yol: Önceki cümle 'fizik bu inancı desteklemiyor' diyor ama NEDENİNİ söylemiyor. Sonraki cümle yüksek yapıların özellikle hedef olduğunu söylüyor. Boşluk ilkeyi vermeli: yıldırım en kolay yolu seçer, o yol yerinde durdukça tekrar seçilir.

p: Many pedestrians press the button at a crossing several times, convinced that it will make the green signal come sooner.
In a number of large cities, however, a large share of these buttons have no effect at all.
Traffic lights in busy areas are often controlled by a central computer that times the signals according to traffic flow, and the buttons were simply left in place when the system was installed.
Similar devices can be found elsewhere: some office thermostats are reported to be dummies, installed to give workers a sense of control over the temperature.
Psychologists point out that people tend to feel less stressed when they believe they have some influence over a situation, even when they do not.
ok: A button that does nothing, then, may still make the wait at the kerb a little easier to bear.

kanca.pw: people tend to feel less stressed

kanca.ow: A button that does nothing, then, may still

d.t: Engineers therefore decided to leave the old buttons exactly where they were when the new central computers were finally installed.
d.key: the buttons were simply left in place
d.bait: decided to leave the old buttons exactly where they were
d.why: Sıra geri gidiyor: düğmelerin yerinde bırakıldığı üçüncü cümlede zaten söylendi. Psikolojik açıklamadan sonra teknik ayrıntıya dönmek kapanışı bozuyor.

d.t: For this reason, cities ought to remove every crossing button that is no longer connected to the signals.
d.key: people tend to feel less stressed
d.why: 'For this reason' önceki cümleden yanlış sonuç çıkarıyor: insanlar kontrol hissiyle rahatlıyorsa bu, düğmeleri sökmek için değil, BIRAKMAK için bir sebep.

d.t: The second experiment, however, found that the calming effect disappeared as soon as people were told the truth.
d.why: 'The second experiment' karşılıksız; paragrafta hiçbir deney anlatılmadı, birincisi bile yok.

d.t: Traffic engineers also lengthen signal timings at some junctions so that elderly pedestrians have more time to cross.
d.bait: elderly pedestrians have more time to cross
d.why: Konu yaşlı yayalara kayıyor. Paragraf 'işe yaramayan düğme neden durur?' sorusunu açıyor; kapanış psikolojik cevabı düğmeye bağlamalı.

yol: Paragraf bir tuhaflıktan (çalışmayan düğmeler) bir açıklamaya (kontrol hissi rahatlatır) gidiyor. Kapanış açıklamayı başa bağlamalı: hiçbir işe yaramayan düğme bile beklemeyi kolaylaştırabilir. 'even when they do not' ile 'does nothing … may still' örtüşüyor.

p: For much of the twentieth century, the appendix was dismissed as a useless leftover of evolution, a small pouch whose only notable feature was its tendency to become inflamed.
Darwin himself had suggested that it was the shrunken remains of a larger organ that our plant-eating ancestors once used to digest leaves.
In 2007 a team at Duke University proposed that it serves as a safe house for helpful gut bacteria, which can recolonise the intestine after an illness such as cholera has flushed them out.
Its tissue is also rich in immune cells, and the organ appears to have evolved independently in many mammal species, which would be odd for something that serves no purpose.
ok: In recent years, however, researchers have begun to suspect that the little organ may have a job after all.

kanca.ow: may have a job after all

kanca.pw: proposed that it serves as a safe house

d.t: Its original function, on this view, had faded away long ago as our ancestors' diet slowly changed.
d.key: the shrunken remains of a larger organ
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Sonraki cümle organa bir İŞLEV önerecek; önce 'eski görüş sorgulanıyor' dönüşü gelmeli.

d.t: Modern research has largely confirmed this view, finding no useful role whatsoever for the organ anywhere in the human body.
d.key: it serves as a safe house for helpful gut bacteria
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki iki cümle organa bir işlev (faydalı bakteri deposu, bağışıklık) öneriyor; 'işe yaramaz' görüşü doğrulanmıyor, sarsılıyor.

d.t: Some studies suggest that people whose appendix has been removed are more likely to suffer repeated gut infections.
d.key: recolonise the intestine after an illness
d.bait: people whose appendix has been removed are more likely
d.why: Zincirde halka atlanıyor: 'bakteri deposu' fikri ortaya atılmadan onu destekleyen bulguya geçiliyor. Önce dönüş, sonra fikir, sonra kanıt gelmeli.

d.t: As a result, the appendix is removed in hundreds of thousands of operations around the world every year.
d.key: Darwin himself had suggested
d.why: 'As a result' önceki cümleye bağlanmıyor: Darwin'in evrim yorumu ameliyatların SEBEBİ değil. Ameliyatlar organın iltihaplanmasından doğuyor.

yol: İlk iki cümle eski görüşü kuruyor (işe yaramaz kalıntı). Sonraki cümle bir ekibin organa İŞLEV önerdiğini söylüyor. Boşluk dönüş noktası olmalı: 'however' ile eski görüş sarsılıyor. Son cümledeki 'something that serves no purpose' de 'a job after all' ile karşılaşıyor.

p: The octopus has a large brain for an invertebrate, but around two thirds of its roughly five hundred million neurons are not in its head at all.
They are spread through its eight arms, each of which contains its own cluster of nerve cells.
In experiments, arms separated from the body have been seen to keep grasping food and passing it towards where the mouth would be.
Some researchers describe the animal as having a central brain that sets goals and a set of semi-independent arms that work out the details.
Such an arrangement is very different from our own, and it raises interesting questions about where, in an octopus, thinking actually happens.
ok: As a result, an arm can taste, touch and even make simple decisions without waiting for instructions from the brain.

kanca.pw: its own cluster of nerve cells
kanca.ow: As a result, an arm can

kanca.pw: arms separated from the body have been seen to keep grasping food
kanca.ow: without waiting for instructions from the brain

d.t: These suckers can each be moved separately, allowing the animal to handle surprisingly small objects with great precision.
d.why: 'These suckers' karşılıksız; paragrafta vantuzdan hiç söz edilmedi.

d.t: Octopuses are also masters of disguise, able to change the colour and texture of their skin in a fraction of a second.
d.why: Konu kamuflaja kayıyor. Paragraf sinir sisteminin kollara dağılmasını izliyor; sonraki cümle kolun kendi başına ne yaptığını gösteriyor.

d.t: Most of the animal's nerve cells, then, lie outside the brain itself, distributed along the length of its limbs.
d.key: spread through its eight arms
d.bait: lie outside the brain itself, distributed along the length of its limbs
d.why: İlk iki cümleyi yineliyor. Sonraki deney bir SONUCU sınıyor (kol kendi başına davranır); önce bu dağılımın ne sağladığı söylenmeli.

d.t: Even so, the arms cannot make the smallest movement unless the brain first sends them detailed instructions.
d.key: semi-independent arms
d.bait: cannot make the smallest movement unless the brain first sends them
d.why: Yön ters. Gövdeden ayrılmış kollar bile yiyecek tutmaya devam ediyor; araştırmacılar kolları 'yarı bağımsız' sayıyor.

yol: Önceki cümle bir yapı veriyor (her kolda ayrı sinir kümesi); sonraki cümle gövdeden ayrılmış kolun bile yiyecek tuttuğunu gösteriyor. Boşluk yapıdan davranışa geçmeli: 'As a result' kol beyinden talimat beklemeden karar verebilir. 'semi-independent arms' bunu doğruluyor.

p: In the winter of 1636 to 1637, the story goes, prices for rare tulip bulbs in the Dutch Republic rose so high that a single bulb could cost as much as a house in Amsterdam.
When prices suddenly collapsed in February 1637, ruined merchants were said to have thrown themselves into canals.
The historian Anne Goldgar, who studied the surviving archives, found little evidence of this.
She could not identify a single person who was bankrupted by tulips, and the trade appears to have involved a relatively small circle of wealthy collectors.
Many of the most dramatic details, it seems, came from moralising pamphlets published after the crash to warn readers against greed.
ok: Tulip mania is often cited as the first financial bubble, a warning of what happens when greed overtakes good sense.

kanca.ow: a warning of what happens when greed overtakes good sense

d.t: Nevertheless, the Dutch Republic was the richest trading nation anywhere in Europe during the seventeenth century.
d.why: Paragraf 'Nevertheless' ile açılamaz; karşı çıkacağı bir önceki söz yok. İçerik de lale hikâyesini tanıtmıyor.

d.t: These bulbs owed their striking streaked petals to a virus, although nobody at the time had any idea of it.
d.why: Paragraf 'These bulbs' ile açılamaz; soğanlar ancak sonraki cümlede anılıyor.

d.t: The pamphlets that spread the legend after the crash were written mainly to warn their Dutch readers against the dangers of greed.
d.key: moralising pamphlets published after the crash
d.bait: The pamphlets that spread the legend
d.why: Paragrafın vardığı sonuç başa konuyor: hangi efsane, hangi çöküş? Efsane ikinci-üçüncü cümlede, çürütülmesi dördüncü-beşincide, broşürler en sonda geliyor.

d.t: A single rare bulb, according to the familiar account, once changed hands for the price of a fine canal house.
d.key: a single bulb could cost as much as a house in Amsterdam
d.bait: once changed hands for the price of a fine canal house
d.why: Sonraki cümle aynı bilgiyi ('a single bulb could cost as much as a house') zaten veriyor; açılış onu önden tekrar ediyor ve konuyu adlandırmıyor.

yol: Boşluk başta. Paragraf bir şöhreti söküyor: 'the story goes' → efsane; tarihçi → kanıt yok; son cümle → hikâye açgözlülüğe karşı uyarmak için yazılmış. Açılış o şöhreti kurmalı: lale çılgınlığı açgözlülük uyarısı olarak anılır. Son cümledeki 'warn readers against greed' bununla çember kapatıyor.

p: Many parents are convinced that sugar makes children hyperactive, and birthday parties full of sweets and screaming seem to prove the point.

Yet when researchers have tested the idea in double-blind trials, in which neither the children nor the adults know who has been given sugar and who a sugar-free substitute, they have found no difference in behaviour.
One study went a step further: mothers were told that their sons had just been given a large dose of sugar, although every child had in fact received a placebo.
Those mothers rated their sons as noticeably more hyperactive and watched them more critically than mothers who had been told nothing.
ok: The hyperactivity, it seems, lies less in the children's blood than in the eyes of the adults watching them.

kanca.pw: Those mothers rated their sons as noticeably more hyperactive
kanca.ow: in the eyes of the adults watching them

kanca.pw: they have found no difference in behaviour
kanca.ow: lies less in the children's blood

d.t: Too much sugar can, of course, contribute to tooth decay and unhealthy weight gain in young children.
d.bait: tooth decay and unhealthy weight gain
d.why: Konu şekerin başka zararlarına kayıyor. Paragraf 'şeker çocuğu hiperaktif yapar mı?' sorusunu cevaplıyor; kapanış o cevaba dönmeli.

d.t: The study therefore confirms that even a small amount of sugar is enough to change a young child's behaviour quite noticeably.
d.key: every child had in fact received a placebo
d.bait: confirms that even a small amount of sugar
d.why: Yön ters. Çocukların hepsi aslında plasebo aldı; değişen çocukların davranışı değil, annelerin yargısıydı.

d.t: For example, children at birthday parties are often tired, overexcited and surrounded by dozens of other children.
d.key: Those mothers rated their sons
d.why: 'For example' önceki cümleye bağlanmıyor: doğum günü partileri annelerin yargısının örneği değil. Paragrafın sonucunu da vermiyor.

d.t: Expecting to see wild behaviour, these mothers judged their sons far more harshly than the other group did.
d.key: watched them more critically
d.bait: judged their sons far more harshly
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Deney anlatıldı; kapanış ondan genel dersi çıkarmalı: sorun çocukta değil, bakan gözde.

yol: Paragraf bir inançtan (şeker hiperaktivite yapar) iki bulguya gidiyor: çift kör denemelerde fark yok; 'şeker verildi' sanan anneler oğullarını daha hareketli görüyor. Kapanış iki bulguyu birleştirmeli: hiperaktivite kanda değil, bakanın gözünde.

p: The shimmering curtains of green and red light seen in polar skies, known as the aurora, begin some 150 million kilometres away, at the sun.
The sun constantly throws out a stream of electrically charged particles, the solar wind, which reaches the Earth after a journey of two to four days.
Near the poles, however, the field lines bend down towards the surface, and some particles are guided into the upper atmosphere.
There they collide with oxygen and nitrogen, which give off light much as the gas in a neon sign does, green and red from oxygen and blue or purple from nitrogen.
During strong solar storms, the aurora can be seen much farther from the poles than usual.
ok: Most of these particles never reach the ground, because the Earth's magnetic field deflects them around the planet like a shield.

kanca.pw: electrically charged particles, the solar wind

d.t: These gases glow in different colours, depending on the height at which the incoming particles strike them.
d.key: oxygen and nitrogen
d.why: 'These gases' henüz anılmadı; oksijen ve azot ancak iki cümle sonra geliyor. Sonraki 'the field lines' de karşılıksız kalıyor.

d.t: The sun is thought to be about halfway through its life and should go on shining for another five billion years or so.
d.why: Konu güneşin ömrüne kayıyor. Sonraki cümle 'the field lines' ve 'however' ile manyetik alanın kutuplardaki istisnasını veriyor; önce alanın genel işi söylenmeli.

d.t: Some of the particles collide with oxygen high in the atmosphere and give off a green glow.
d.key: There they collide with oxygen and nitrogen
d.bait: collide with oxygen high in the atmosphere
d.why: Zincirde halka atlanıyor: parçacıkların atmosfere nasıl girdiği (manyetik alan, kutuplar) söylenmeden çarpışmaya geçiliyor. Bu adım beşinci cümlenin işi.

d.t: The Earth's magnetic field draws these particles straight down towards the surface, wherever on the planet they happen to arrive.
d.key: Near the poles, however, the field lines bend down
d.bait: wherever on the planet they happen to arrive
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki 'Near the poles, however' bir istisna veriyor: yalnız kutuplarda parçacıklar içeri yönlendiriliyor. Demek ki alan genelde onları SAPTIRIYOR, her yerde içeri çekmiyor.

yol: Sonraki cümle 'Near the poles, however' ile bir istisna veriyor ve 'the field lines' diyor: boşlukta manyetik alanın GENEL kuralı olmalı. Önceki cümle parçacıkları getirdi; boşluk onların çoğunun alan tarafından saptırıldığını söylemeli. İstisna (kutuplar) ancak böyle anlam kazanıyor.

p: In a series of experiments published in 2011, researchers asked volunteers to assemble simple storage boxes from flat-pack kits, while others were given identical boxes already built.
When both groups were then asked how much they would pay for the boxes, the builders offered considerably more than those who had done no work.
Their pride, however, depended on success: when participants were given kits they could not complete, or were made to take their boxes apart again, the extra value disappeared.
The researchers called this pattern the IKEA effect, after the Swedish furniture company whose customers assemble their own purchases.
Some companies may benefit from it simply by leaving a small part of the job to the customer.
ok: Their own labour, it seemed, had made them strangely fond of what were really quite ordinary objects.

kanca.ow: strangely fond of what were really quite ordinary objects

d.t: The researchers named the finding after a Swedish company whose customers put together their own furniture at home.
d.key: called this pattern the IKEA effect
d.bait: named the finding after a Swedish company
d.why: Adlandırma öne alınıyor. Önce bulgunun sebebi (emek bağlılık yaratır), sonra sınırı (başarı şart), en son adı gelmeli; sonraki 'Their pride' de bu cümlede gurur bulamıyor.

d.t: Similarly, the people who had built nothing were happy to pay the full price for a ready-made box.
d.key: the builders offered considerably more than those who had done no work
d.why: 'Similarly' (benzer şekilde) yanlış: hazır kutu alanlar kurucuların TERSİNE daha az teklif etti. İki grup arasında benzerlik değil, fark var.

d.t: The effort of building, it seemed, had actually made people like their boxes rather less than before.
d.key: the builders offered considerably more
d.why: Yön ters. Kurucular kutulara DAHA ÇOK değer biçti; sonraki 'Their pride' de bir gurur, yani artı bir duygu bekliyor.

d.t: Those who had assembled the boxes themselves were willing to spend noticeably more money on them.
d.key: the builders offered considerably more than those who had done no work
d.bait: willing to spend noticeably more money
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Bulgu zaten verildi; sonraki 'Their pride' bu bulgunun ARDINDAKİ duyguyu (emeğe bağlılık) bekliyor.

yol: Önceki cümle bir bulgu veriyor (kurucular daha çok ödemeye razı). Sonraki cümle 'Their pride, however' ile o duygunun sınırını çiziyor. Boşluk bulgudan duyguya geçmeli: emek, sıradan bir nesneyi sevdirdi. 'Their own labour' ile 'Their pride' yan yana oturuyor.

p: Alcohol-based hand gels have become a familiar sight in hospitals, offices and shops, and for many germs they work extremely well.
Alcohol destroys bacteria and many viruses by breaking down their outer membranes, often within seconds.
Norovirus, the cause of many outbreaks of vomiting on cruise ships and in care homes, belongs to this group and is only weakly affected by most gels.
The spores of the bacterium Clostridioides difficile, which causes severe diarrhoea in hospital patients, are similarly hard to kill.
Against these, health authorities recommend old-fashioned soap and water, which does not need to kill germs because the rubbing and rinsing simply wash them off the skin.
ok: Some viruses, however, have no such membrane at all, leaving the alcohol with very little to attack.

kanca.ow: have no such membrane at all

kanca.pw: only weakly affected by most gels

d.t: These spores can survive on hospital surfaces for many months, waiting for a new host to come along.
d.key: The spores of the bacterium
d.why: 'These spores' henüz anılmadı; sporlar ancak iki cümle sonra geliyor. Sonraki 'this group' de bu cümlede bir grup bulamıyor.

d.t: Many people also find that frequent use of the gels leaves their skin dry and cracked.
d.bait: leaves their skin dry and cracked
d.why: Konu cilt kuruluğuna kayıyor. Sonraki cümle 'this group' diyerek alkolün etkisiz kaldığı bir mikrop GRUBU bekliyor.

d.t: Soap and water, which simply wash germs away rather than killing them, are therefore a better choice for some infections.
d.key: health authorities recommend old-fashioned soap and water
d.why: Çözüm sorundan önce geliyor: jelin hangi mikroplarda yetersiz kaldığı söylenmeden sabuna geçiliyor. Bu son cümlenin işi; 'therefore' da dayanaksız.

d.t: As a result, hospital infections caused by viruses have almost disappeared since the gels were introduced.
d.key: Norovirus, the cause of many outbreaks
d.why: 'As a result' önceki cümleden fazla büyük bir sonuç çıkarıyor; sonraki cümle de norovirüs salgınlarının sürdüğünü söylüyor. Sebep-sonuç bağı kurulamıyor.

yol: Önceki cümle alkolün nasıl çalıştığını söylüyor: dış zarı parçalıyor. Sonraki cümle norovirüsün 'bu gruba' girdiğini ve jelden az etkilendiğini söylüyor. Boşluk o grubu tanımlamalı: zarı OLMAYAN virüsler. 'such membrane' önceki cümleye, 'Some viruses' sonraki 'this group' ifadesine bağlanıyor.

p: The flightless bird lived only on Mauritius, an island in the Indian Ocean that had no human inhabitants and no large land predators until Dutch sailors arrived in 1598.
Having evolved without enemies, the dodo showed little fear of people, which early visitors took as a sign of stupidity.
Hunting played a part in its decline, but sailors found the meat tough and unpleasant, and many historians now place more of the blame on the animals that came ashore with them.
Rats, pigs and monkeys raided the nests the birds built on the ground, eating their eggs and chicks.
Within less than a century the dodo was gone.
ok: The dodo is remembered as a symbol of extinction and, unfairly, of foolishness, but its story is more complicated.

kanca.pw: early visitors took as a sign of stupidity
many historians now place more of the blame

d.t: These animals soon multiplied, since nothing on the island preyed on them and food was easy to find.
d.why: Paragraf 'These animals' ile açılamaz; hangi hayvanlar? Gemilerle gelen fareler, domuzlar ve maymunlar ancak beşinci cümlede anılıyor.

d.t: As a result, Mauritius is today one of the most densely populated countries anywhere in Africa.
d.why: Paragraf 'As a result' ile açılamaz; neyin sonucu? İçerik de dodo hikâyesini tanıtmıyor; sonraki 'The flightless bird' karşılıksız kalıyor.

d.t: Few extinctions are as simple to explain as that of the dodo, which was eaten by hungry sailors.
d.key: sailors found the meat tough and unpleasant
d.why: Yön ters. Paragraf avlanmanın tek sebep OLMADIĞINI, denizcilerin eti sevmediğini ve suçun gemilerle gelen hayvanlarda olduğunu anlatıyor.

d.t: The dodo, a large bird that could not fly, was found nowhere else but on one island in the Indian Ocean.
d.key: lived only on Mauritius
d.bait: found nowhere else but on one island
d.why: Sonraki cümle aynı bilgiyi (uçamayan kuş, yalnız Mauritius'ta) zaten veriyor; açılış onu önden tekrar ediyor. Paragrafın tezi (hikâye sanıldığından karmaşık) kurulmuyor.

yol: Boşluk başta. Sonraki cümle 'The flightless bird' diyor: kuş açılışta adıyla anılmalı. Paragraf iki önyargıyı düzeltiyor: dodo aptal değildi (korkusuzluğu düşmansız evrimden), yok oluşu da yalnız avdan değildi. Açılış bu iki önyargıyı ve 'daha karmaşık' tezini haber veriyor.

p: In a 1993 study, the psychologist Anders Ericsson found that the best violin students at a Berlin music academy had practised for an average of about ten thousand hours by the age of twenty.
Years later, a best-selling book turned the figure into a simple rule: ten thousand hours of practice is what it takes to master any skill.
Ericsson himself objected to this reading.

The number was only an average, many of the students had practised far less, and what mattered, he argued, was not the hours themselves but deliberate practice, focused on specific weaknesses and guided by expert feedback.
Later studies have also found that practice explains only part of the differences between performers, with factors such as starting age and talent playing a role.
ok: Hours alone, it seems, are neither a guarantee of mastery nor the whole of the story.

kanca.pw: explains only part of the differences
kanca.ow: nor the whole of the story

kanca.pw: what it takes to master any skill

d.t: The violin is often considered one of the most difficult instruments to learn, especially for adult beginners.
d.why: Konu kemanın zorluğuna kayıyor. Keman yalnız çalışmanın örneklemi; paragraf 'on bin saat kuralı'nı sorguluyor ve kapanış o kurala dönmeli.

d.t: A best-selling book would later turn this figure into a simple rule that has been widely repeated ever since.
d.key: a best-selling book turned the figure into a simple rule
d.bait: would later turn this figure into a simple rule
d.why: Sıra geri gidiyor: kitabın kuralı ikinci cümlede zaten anlatıldı ve sonra çürütüldü. Çürütmeden sonra kuralın doğuşuna dönmek kapanışı bozuyor.

d.t: Ten thousand hours, these later studies confirm, is the point at which almost anyone becomes an expert in a field.
d.key: practice explains only part of the differences
d.bait: the point at which almost anyone becomes an expert
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki çalışmalar pratiğin farkların ancak BİR KISMINI açıkladığını buldu; Ericsson da saatlerin tek başına belirleyici olmadığını söyledi.

d.t: Natural ability and the age at which a person starts, it seems, also make a real difference.
d.key: factors such as starting age and talent playing a role
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Kapanış iki itirazı (Ericsson'un 'bilinçli pratik' itirazı ve sonraki çalışmalar) birleştirip kurala bir hüküm vermeli.

yol: Paragraf bir kuralı iki yönden sorguluyor: Ericsson 'saat değil, bilinçli pratik' diyor; sonraki çalışmalar 'pratik farkın yalnız bir kısmı' diyor. Kapanış ikisini toplamalı: saatler ne ustalığı garanti eder (Ericsson) ne de hikâyenin tamamıdır (yeni çalışmalar).

p: Brain-training apps promise that a few minutes of puzzles a day will sharpen memory, attention and reasoning.
Users certainly get better at the games: after a few weeks, their scores on the trained tasks usually rise steeply.
A large review published in 2016 concluded that improvements rarely spread to other tasks, and almost never to the demands of everyday life.
Someone who becomes skilled at remembering sequences of coloured squares, for example, will not necessarily find it easier to remember where they left their keys.
In the same year, one leading company agreed to pay two million dollars in the United States to settle charges that its advertising had been misleading.
ok: The crucial question, though, is whether these gains carry over to anything beyond the games themselves.

kanca.pw: their scores on the trained tasks usually rise
improvements rarely spread to other tasks
kanca.ow: carry over to anything beyond the games

d.t: These coloured squares flash on the screen for less than a second before vanishing again.
d.key: sequences of coloured squares
d.why: 'These coloured squares' henüz anılmadı; renkli kareler ancak iki cümle sonra örnek olarak geliyor.

d.t: As a result, the companies behind them can fairly claim that their products make people cleverer.
d.key: their scores on the trained tasks usually rise steeply
d.why: 'As a result' yanlış bir sonuç çıkarıyor: oyunda puanın artması, insanın genel olarak zekileşmesi demek değil. Sonraki cümle de bu iddiayı çürütüyor.

d.t: Many of the games are designed by teams of programmers who also work on popular video games.
d.bait: also work on popular video games
d.why: Konu oyunları tasarlayanlara kayıyor. Sonraki cümle bir SORUYA cevap veriyor (gelişme başka işlere yayılıyor mu?); önce o soru sorulmalı.

d.t: The answer to that, according to a major review of the research, appears to be largely no.
d.key: A large review published in 2016 concluded
d.why: Cevap sorudan önce geliyor: 'The answer to that' neyin cevabı? Soru sorulmadı. İnceleme de zaten sonraki cümlede anlatılıyor.

yol: Önceki cümle 'certainly' ile bir şeyi kabul ediyor (oyunda gelişiyorlar); bu kabul bir 'ama' habercisi. Sonraki cümle 'gelişme başka işlere nadiren yayılıyor' diye bir CEVAP veriyor. Boşluk soruyu sormalı: bu kazançlar oyunun dışına taşıyor mu?

p: In 1963 Erasto Mpemba, a schoolboy in Tanzania, noticed that the hot ice-cream mixture he put in the freezer froze before the cool mixture of his classmates.
His teacher dismissed the observation, but Mpemba persisted, and in 1969 he and a physicist published a paper describing the effect.
Hot water evaporates faster, losing mass, and it may contain less dissolved gas, and either of these might in principle speed up freezing.

Yet attempts to reproduce the effect have given conflicting results, partly because the outcome depends heavily on the shape of the container, the freezer and even the exact moment at which water is counted as frozen.
A 2016 analysis concluded that there was no convincing evidence for it.
ok: Since then, scientists have proposed a number of explanations for why hot water might freeze faster than cold.

kanca.pw: published a paper describing the effect
might in principle speed up freezing
Yet attempts to reproduce the effect
kanca.ow: why hot water might freeze faster

d.t: Since then, careful experiments have repeatedly and convincingly confirmed that hot water freezes faster than cold water does.
d.key: attempts to reproduce the effect have given conflicting results
d.why: Yön ters. Sondan bir önceki cümle denemelerin ÇELİŞKİLİ sonuç verdiğini, son cümle de ikna edici kanıt olmadığını söylüyor.

d.t: Despite his teacher's scepticism, the young student kept investigating until the effect was finally described in print.
d.key: Mpemba persisted
d.bait: kept investigating until the effect was finally described in print
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Sonraki cümle olası mekanizmaları (buharlaşma, gaz) sayıyor; önce 'açıklamalar önerildi' diye bir giriş gerekiyor.

d.t: This gas forms tiny bubbles that make the finished ice look cloudy rather than perfectly clear.
d.key: dissolved gas
d.why: 'This gas' karşılıksız; çözünmüş gaz ancak sonraki cümlede anılıyor.

d.t: For example, the Greek philosopher Aristotle had described something very similar more than two thousand years earlier.
d.key: in 1969 he and a physicist published a paper
d.why: 'For example' önceki cümleye bağlanmıyor: Aristoteles'in gözlemi makalenin yayımlanmasının örneği değil. Sonraki cümledeki açıklamalara da köprü kurmuyor.

yol: Sonraki cümle iki olası mekanizmayı (hızlı buharlaşma, az gaz) 'might in principle' temkiniyle sayıyor: demek ki boşluk açıklama arayışını BAŞLATMALI. Önceki cümle 1969 makalesiyle bitiyor; 'Since then' oradan devralıyor. 'might freeze faster' de son iki cümledeki şüpheye uygun.

p: The claim appeared in print long before anyone had been into space, and it has been repeated in textbooks, quiz books and travel guides ever since.
Astronauts who have orbited the Earth, however, report that the wall is extremely hard to make out with the naked eye.
Although it is very long, it is only a few metres wide, and it is built from materials that are similar in colour to the land around it.
Motorways and airports, which are both wider and more sharply contrasted with their surroundings, are far easier to see.
In 2003 even China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, admitted that he had not been able to spot it.
ok: A much-repeated fact about the Great Wall of China is that it can be seen from space.

kanca.pw: repeated in textbooks, quiz books and travel guides
the wall is extremely hard to make out
kanca.ow: it can be seen from space

d.t: Even China's first astronaut admitted, on returning to Earth, that he had not been able to find the wall.
d.key: even China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, admitted
d.why: 'Even' (bile) bir zincirin son halkasıdır; paragraf onunla açılamaz. İddia, astronotların gözlemi ve sebepler önce gelmeli; bu cümle son cümlenin işi.

d.t: Few structures built by human beings stand out from orbit as clearly as the Great Wall of China.
d.key: the wall is extremely hard to make out
d.bait: stand out from orbit as clearly
d.why: Yön ters. Astronotlar duvarın çıplak gözle ZOR seçildiğini söylüyor; otoyollar ve havaalanları ondan çok daha kolay görünüyor.

d.t: However, the Great Wall was actually built over many centuries by a number of different Chinese dynasties.
d.why: Paragraf 'However' ile açılamaz; karşı çıkacağı bir önceki söz yok. İçerik de sonraki 'The claim' için bir iddia kurmuyor.

d.t: This structure stretches for thousands of kilometres across the hills and deserts of northern China.
d.why: Paragraf 'This structure' ile açılamaz; hangi yapı? Duvar henüz adlandırılmadı. Sonraki 'The claim' de bir iddia bulamıyor.

yol: Boşluk başta. Sonraki cümle 'The claim' diyor ve bunun kitaplarda tekrarlandığını söylüyor: açılış bir İDDİA kurmalı. Üçüncü cümle 'the wall' diyor ve görülmesinin zor olduğunu söylüyor: iddia 'uzaydan görülür'. 'much-repeated' ile 'repeated in textbooks' örtüşüyor.

p: Spinach is famous for its iron, a reputation often credited with turning the cartoon sailor Popeye into its most enthusiastic advertiser.
In fact, spinach contains no more iron than many other green vegetables, and much of it is bound to oxalic acid, which makes it hard for the body to absorb.
For decades this explanation was itself repeated in books and lectures as a cautionary tale about careless science.
In 2010, however, the criminologist Mike Sutton traced the sources and found no evidence that any such decimal error had ever occurred.
The myth about the myth, it turned out, had spread just as easily as the original one.
ok: A popular story blamed the mistake on a misplaced decimal point that made spinach seem ten times richer in iron.

kanca.ow: A popular story blamed the mistake
seem ten times richer in iron

d.t: Spinach is also rich in vitamin K, which the body needs in order to help the blood clot after an injury.
d.why: Konu K vitaminine kayıyor. Sonraki 'this explanation' bir AÇIKLAMA bekliyor: ıspanağın ünü nereden geldi?

d.t: Its iron, in addition, is not easily taken up by the body because of a substance it contains.
d.key: makes it hard for the body to absorb
d.bait: is not easily taken up by the body
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor (oksalik asit emilimi zorlaştırıyor). Sonraki 'this explanation' ve 'decimal error' bir hata hikâyesi bekliyor.

d.t: Its iron content is in reality far higher than that of almost any other vegetable grown in Europe.
d.key: contains no more iron than many other green vegetables
d.bait: far higher than that of almost any other vegetable
d.why: Yön ters. Önceki cümle ıspanağın diğer yeşil sebzelerden FAZLA demir içermediğini söylüyor.

d.t: A careful search through the original sources, however, turned up nothing at all to support the tale.
d.key: traced the sources and found no evidence
d.bait: A careful search through the original sources
d.why: Çürütme hikâyeden önce geliyor: 'the tale' henüz anlatılmadı. Kaynak taraması beşinci cümlenin işi; önce ondalık hata hikâyesi kurulmalı.

yol: Sonraki cümle 'this explanation' diyor, beşinci cümle de 'any such decimal error'. Demek ki boşluk bir AÇIKLAMA vermeli ve içinde ondalık hata olmalı. Önceki cümle ıspanağın ününün hak edilmediğini söyledi; boşluk bu yanlışın nereden geldiğine dair yaygın hikâyeyi anlatıyor.

p: Young sunflower plants follow the sun across the sky, facing east in the morning and turning slowly west as the day goes on.
During the night they swing back to the east, ready for the next sunrise.
A study published in 2016 found that this movement is controlled by an internal clock: the east side of the stem grows faster during the day and the west side grows faster at night.
Once the plants mature and their flowers open, however, the tracking stops, and almost all of them stay facing east.
The researchers found that east-facing flowers warm up faster in the morning sun and receive around five times as many visits from bees as flowers turned to the west.
ok: Facing the sunrise, it seems, is not a habit left over from youth but a way of attracting pollinators.

kanca.pw: receive around five times as many visits from bees
Young sunflower plants follow the sun
kanca.ow: a habit left over from youth

d.t: In contrast, a warm flower is more attractive to bees, which much prefer to feed in comfortable conditions in the morning.
d.key: east-facing flowers warm up faster
d.why: 'In contrast' (aksine) yanlış: bu cümle önceki bulguyla çelişmiyor, onu AÇIKLIYOR. Kapanış da doğu yönünün neden korunduğuna bir hüküm vermiyor.

d.t: Sunflower seeds are also an important source of cooking oil in countries such as Ukraine, Russia and Argentina.
d.bait: an important source of cooking oil
d.why: Konu ayçiçeği yağına kayıyor. Paragraf çiçeğin neden doğuya baktığını soruyor; kapanış o soruya cevap vermeli.

d.t: Bees, the study showed, much prefer the flowers that have already been warmed by the early morning sun.
d.key: east-facing flowers warm up faster in the morning sun
d.bait: much prefer the flowers that have already been warmed
d.why: Önceki cümleyi yineliyor. Bulgu zaten verildi; kapanış onu baştaki genç bitkilerin güneşi izlemesiyle karşılaştırıp anlamını söylemeli.

d.t: This second clock, the researchers believe, controls the moment at which the flower itself begins to open.
d.key: controlled by an internal clock
d.why: 'This second clock' var olmayan bir şeye dönüyor: paragrafta yalnız BİR iç saat anılıyor.

yol: Paragraf iki dönemi karşılaştırıyor: gençken güneşi izleme (iç saat), olgunken hep doğuya bakma. Son cümle doğuya bakmanın yararını (sıcaklık, 5 kat arı) veriyor. Kapanış bunu yorumlamalı: doğuya bakmak gençlikten kalma bir alışkanlık değil, tozlayıcı çekme yolu.

p: On 18 August 1913, at the casino in Monte Carlo, the ball on a roulette wheel landed on black again and again.
As the streak grew longer, gamblers began betting ever larger sums on red, convinced that the wheel was now overdue to change.
By the time red finally came up, the ball had fallen on black twenty-six times in a row, and the casino had won millions of francs.
The gamblers' mistake, now known as the gambler's fallacy or the Monte Carlo fallacy, is to treat independent events as if they were connected.
A roulette wheel has no memory, and each spin gives black and red the same chance as before.
ok: Yet the wheel kept producing black, and with every spin the losses on red grew heavier and heavier.

kanca.pw: betting ever larger sums on red
kanca.ow: the losses on red grew heavier
Yet the wheel kept producing black

kanca.pw: By the time red finally came up

d.t: In the end, the ball would land on black twenty-six times in a row before red finally appeared.
d.key: twenty-six times in a row
d.why: Sonuç öne alınıyor: serinin nasıl bittiği sonraki cümlenin işi. Arada bahislerin nasıl battığı halkası atlanıyor ve sonraki cümle aynı bilgiyi tekrar etmek zorunda kalıyor.

d.t: Within a few spins red came up, and the gamblers who had bet on it won a fortune.
d.key: the ball had fallen on black twenty-six times in a row
d.bait: Within a few spins red came up
d.why: Yön ters. Sonraki cümle kırmızının ancak 26 siyahtan sonra geldiğini ve KASİNONUN milyonlar kazandığını söylüyor.

d.t: Surely, they reasoned, red was bound to come up sooner or later after such a long run of black.
d.key: convinced that the wheel was now overdue to change
d.bait: red was bound to come up
d.why: Önceki cümledeki inancı yineliyor. Sonraki 'By the time red finally came up' bekleyişin UZADIĞINI ve kayıpları varsayıyor; o halka eksik.

d.t: Roulette itself is thought to have developed in eighteenth-century France from a number of older wheel games.
d.why: Konu ruletin tarihine kayıyor. Paragraf o geceki seriyi ve kumarbazların yanılgısını izliyor.

yol: Önceki cümle bir beklenti kuruyor (artık kırmızı gelmeli, bahisler büyüyor). Sonraki cümle 'By the time red finally came up' diyor: demek ki arada beklenti BOŞA çıkmaya devam etmeli. Boşluk: 'Yet' siyah gelmeye devam etti, kırmızıdaki kayıplar büyüdü.
